courses.5f4j:
Students will benefit from a broad introduction to commerce, exploring the various functions found within almost all businesses – from operations to marketing, accounting and human resource management. Students will develop an understanding of how and where businesses sell their products and services, who they sell to, how they make decisions, and what improves their chances of success.

This course can be studied full-time over three years, or four years if students choose to add a placement year in industry. There’s also a two and a half-year accelerated option, and a part-time option. There are intakes in October and January.
courses.5f4v:
The course is the ideal springboard for those who are looking for a successful management career in one of the world’s fastest-growing industries. Hospitality and tourism offer exciting career opportunities because, despite the broader economic outlook, these industries continue to thrive around the world – and employers are always looking for accomplished graduates. This exciting, fast-paced and highly practical course will prepare students for a wide range of management and leadership positions, all with a global perspective and within a multi-cultural environment.

Students will engage regularly with top employers and there are multiple opportunities to explore the industries in action. And where better to study than Coventry's London campus, surrounded by some of the world’s most iconic hotels and attractions, which are visited by over 32 million tourists a year?

courses.5f4h:
Where better to study financial economics and banking than London, one of the world’s leading financial centres? At Coventry's London campus, students will be surrounded by hundreds of financial institutions. We’re just a few minutes’ walk from the traditional financial district (which includes the Bank of England and the London Stock Exchange) and we’re also within view of Canary Wharf, the new financial district in East London. The department will arrange visits to these centres, and students may apply to have the opportunity to do an internship there.

This course provides the ideal blend of academic theory and hands-on experience. In class, students will work on practical exercises such as case studies and business, banking or trading simulations. They will be taught to do real workplace tasks using industry-standard technology, and we encourage contact with financial firms which may be through work experience and visits to companies and institutions.

courses.1gpu:
Program Description

This highly practical course has been designed with the future in mind. Taking into consideration growing disciplines such as artificial intelligence, students will study several defined business areas that reflect the ever-changing needs of the market. These include modules such as Digital Transformation and Innovation in Business and Ethical and Responsible Leadership.

Employability is at the heart of De Montfort University's Business Management course. Alongside the opportunity of a year-long placement, students will also work on integrated case studies, which will give students the opportunity to hear from and gain insight into global brands such as Apple and Amazon. Students will step away from the confines of their text books and apply their theoretical knowledge to practical business simulations set by executives from these global businesses.

Students will receive an excellent grounding in all aspects of business management, incorporating knowledge from a range of disciplines such as accounting, economics, finance, human resource management, marketing, and sustainability.

A Business Management degree at DMU can open up an exciting career path in a wide range of specialist areas such as project consulting, project management, and digital transformation. Previous graduates from this degree have gone on to successful careers in world-renowned organisations, including Amazon, Goldman Sachs, Caterpillar, HP and The Body Shop.

Key features:

  • Gain real-time insights on the state of global companies, in the past students have worked with executives from companies such as Amazon and Apple, through integrated case studies and business simulations.
  • De Montfort University's 'In Business With' initiative brings business leaders into your classroom to give students a better understanding of how business works in the real world. Students will have the opportunity to learn about their success and failures which students can then apply to their future career.
  • Benefit from guest lecture series run by executives from popular blue-chip companies, in previous years De Montfort University has had the likes of Amazon, Apple and contestants from the apprentice.
  • Students will be provided with an excellent grounding in all aspects of business which will give them the ability to critically evaluate organisations in terms of their key areas of business management, structures, functions, and processes.
  • Develop the values, skills, knowledge, and behaviours that will enable students to contribute to the development of a just, peaceful, and sustainable world through the Contemporary Issues in Sustainable Business module.
  • Students have secured year-long placements in companies such as BMW, Jaguar Land Rover and Siemens, through De Montfort University's Works careers and employability team who provide exceptional support that will help students plan their career path.
  • Through block teaching, students will focus on one subject at a time instead of several at once. This means that students will be able to focus closely on each subject and absorb their learning material in more depth, whilst working more closely with their tutors and course mates.

courses.1gtm:
Program Description

Study a variety of business functions in an international context and learn about the complexities involved in conducting business overseas

This course will appeal to those with an understanding and exploring how organisations compete and co-operate around the world. The course focuses on organisational activity and the supporting regulatory, legislative and political environments that help facilitate trade between companies and across international boundaries.

Reasons to study International Business at DMU

  • Students will gain a global perspective on businesses and their activities across the world
  • Pitch a business idea to real-life entrepreneurs and win a great prize through the annual Fox’s Lair competition for first year students
  • Enjoy an international experience with #DMUglobal: The innovative programme of work and study opportunities across the world, which can enrich studies and expand cultural horizons
  • Learn the latest developments in business practice: Lecturers draw on their extensive experience and many are involved in consultancy and training with large organisations in the private and public sectors
  • Innovative assessments help students to develop skills which are highly sought after by employers: Build confidence and enhance creative, organisational and communication skills
  • Placement opportunities with local, national and global companies including Rolls Royce, IBM, Walt Disney, the NHS and Siemens
  • Alumni are employed by leading brands in graduate roles such as Business Analyst at Capita, Supply Manager at Cummins, General Management Graduate at Network Rail and Business Process and Design Analyst at Vodafone
courses.1gp6:
This course is ideal for students interested in a professional career in accounting and want to maximize the number of exemptions from professional body exams.

Close links with employers and professional accounting bodies ensure students have the opportunity to enhance their future career prospects and gain up to nine exemptions from the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), the maximum number available, as well as exemptions from CIMA, CII, ACT, AIA, CFA, CIPFA, ICAEW and the CPA.

DMU's Bloomberg Trading Room – one of the largest in a UK university – will give students a simulated experience on industry-standard software that is used by decision-makers in finance.

Key features

  • 96% of the Accounting and Finance graduates from summer 2017 are in work or further study after graduating (Destination of Leavers from Higher Education (DLHE) 2016-17).
  • DMU is a Gold Status ACCA Learning Partner and are accredited by CIMA.
  • DMU graduates have gone on to careers in globally renowned organisations. Recent successes include Barclays, Ernst & Young, IBM, PwC and many more.
  • Enjoy an international experience with #DMUglobal – on these trips students will visit sites like Wall Street which give them a real-world experience that applies directly to their studies.
  • Module content is broad in nature, covering a multitude of topics including Management Accounting, Corporate Finance, Management and Strategy, Forensic Accounting and Advanced Financial Reporting.
courses.1gph:
Program Description

Studying Architecture offers students the opportunity to pursue a career in an exciting, creative and fast-paced industry which hugely influences the world around us.

On this course students will discover how to bring their visions and designs to life, with successful graduates progressing into rewarding careers which have the potential to improve and enhance the lives of countless people. With the knowledge gained as part of this degree, can witness their work turn into tangible creations that serve the communities around them.

Students will learn about the history of architecture and design, alongside completing technical, practical and professional exercises relating to ethical architecture in the commercial world. Student will have opportunities to undertake design projects in a range of spatial, social and topographical settings, from the smallest of residences and objects through to complex megacities and events.

This course is a professionally validated undergraduate degree which prepares students for a postgraduate degree in Architecture, which most graduates will progress to. Graduates pursue successful careers in non-professional pathways using their skills in creative design, strategic thinking, leadership and organisation.

The course is on the Commonwealth Association of Architects’ approved courses list.

Key features

  • This course is accredited by the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) and the Architects Registration Board (ARB), ensuring the content students study meets and exceeds the criteria set out by these professional bodies, with students also exempt from RIBA and ARB Part I examinations.
  • This course benefits from global opportunities thanks to its accreditation with Lembaga Arkitek Malaysia (LAM), the Board of Architects Malaysia, which allows graduates to pursue a professional qualification in Malaysia. It is also approved by the Commonwealth Association of Architects, a membership organisation representing architects in Commonwealth countries, which provides access to an international network of schools for further study and better employment prospects.
  • DMU’s Leicester School of Architecture - is only one of five schools of architecture in the world to win more than three RIBA Part II design awards in the past five years. It’s also one of the oldest architecture schools in the UK, established in 1897, allowing students to draw on a wealth of experience and expertise.
  • Students gain valuable international experience as part of their studies with DMU Global programme. Previous trips have taken students overseas to work on live projects in Berlin in collaboration with Aedas, a leading international architecture and design practice. Students have also travelled to destinations such as Ahmedabad, India, where they designed and built homes to help those living in disadvantaged communities.
  • DMU is ranked in number one for Architecture in the East Midlands for 'Graduate Prospectus', according to The Complete University Guide 2020, many of our graduates have gone on to work for some of the best architectural practices in the UK and worldwide, including Heatherwick Studio, Make Architects and Shigeru Ban Architects.
  • Benefit from the very latest facilities – dedicated multipurpose studios, CAD labs, workshops offering metal working and woodworking to digital printing and water-jet cutting and prototype workshops. DMU's award-winning Vijay Patel Building provides both the space and the facilities to foster creative thinking and explore design potential.
  • DMU provides core workshop materials at no cost, and gives cash awards – £150, £200 and £300 in years one, two and three respectively – to support personal materials/printing costs
courses.1gsr:
Program Description

On this course students develop their skills as a professional film-maker, critic, event organiser, writer or industry analyst through the academic study of cinema, to prepare them for a career in the creative industries.

In an increasingly media-focused world, this course will develop your existing passion for film and TV into a prospective career, helping you acquire a skillset required for many technical and creative roles.

From broadcast journalism to the arts and events, this course focuses on the study of film and its variety of uses, and challenges students to see far beyond just the viewing experience.

Students will be able to choose modules that combine practice and study, giving students a strong theoretical understanding, as well as versatile skills such as communication and critical analysis. Graduates go on to work in a variety of fields, including film and TV, but also finance, public relations, banking, and tourism.

Key features

  • Gain a strong theoretical understanding of the global film industry, cult film, media capture and processing, audiences and fandom, writing for the screen, and the practical skills of film-making.
  • Learn in a real cinema environment thanks to our partnership with Leicester’s Phoenix Cinema and Arts Centre, while benefiting from placement opportunities and the chance to organise and manage an annual film festival.
  • Gain valuable international experience with the #DMUglobal programme. Students have been able to immerse themselves in Hollywood’s fan culture, tour iconic cinemas in Berlin and attend the famous Cannes Film Festival.
  • Benefit from experts in prestigious Cinema and Television History Research Institute, as well as guest lectures by well-established film directors, exhibitors, writers, distributors, and journalists.
  • Communication, cultural and media studies research is ranked joint first in the UK for the proportion of research outputs, rated as world-leading (4*) in the Research Excellence Framework 2014, the most recent evaluation of its kind.
  • Graduates have gone on to work for high-profile employers including the BBC and Odeon Entertainment in varied roles including research, teaching and writing for film, public relations and film journalism.

Program Description

These days, accounting is about so much more than crunching numbers. Accountancy is complex, and brings into play a number of expert skills.

Students will learn and develop a combination of accounting, finance and other business skills including accounting techniques and policies relating to corporate finance, tax, auditing, corporate governance, management accounting, corporate reporting and statistics.

Students will offer tuition that is supported by experienced teaching staff with strong industry connections. Guest speakers from the public and private sectors add value to the course. In addition, transferable skills of time management, project management, communication, collection and management of data and IT skills will serve them well in the future, whatever their career choice.
courses.4n1e:
Program Description

Accounting is more than just number crunching.

On this accredited courses students will learn and develop a combination of accounting, finance and other business skills.

Students are accredited by major UK accounting institutes and this highly regarded course will prepare them for a range of careers in accounting or further study.

All the Joint Honours Accounting degrees involve the same compulsory accounting modules but concentrate students' option choices into a specialised route.

Students will study six modules, over two trimesters, per year. They'll learn by a variety of teaching methods including lectures, tutorials, workshops, directed learning and independent study.

On successful completion of Year 3, students will be eligible for an unclassified degree, and on successful completion of Year 4, an Honours degree.
courses.4n1j:
Program Description

This Business Management course provides students with opportunities to discover how all organisations are managed, and develop and grow.

Students will explore the internal structures and strategies which businesses adopt in response to the key external drivers for change which impact upon them.

With flexible study options and practical content, the aim of the BA (Hons) Business Management is to offer a number of major/minor combinations which take advantage of the flexibility of the modular structure and promote student choice. This course provides modules that give students real-world experience and the option to undertake a work placement.

92% of graduates were in work or further study within 6 months of graduating in 2018.
courses.4n1k:
Program Description

This Business Management with Entrepreneurship course combines a broad range of academic theory in the area of business management with the latest applied thinking in the field of entrepreneurship.

This course provides modules that give students real-world experience and the option to undertake a work placement.

This will prepare students for a range of projects and careers with small, medium and large employers, or for venturing out on their own.

In the first two years students will build a foundation in the essentials of effective business management. This foundation prepares students for the options to engage with applied learning within an industry placement, or to explore diverse cultures through studying abroad within the extensive partner network.

This course offers students excellent employability skills including professional presentation, team working, leadership, communication and problem solving.
courses.4n1m:
Program Description

The Business Management with Marketing course combines broad ranging business knowledge with strategic marketing competencies.

This course provides modules that give students real-world experience and the option to undertake a work placement.

The course will further advance students' creative and innovative skills to successfully market and promote themselves across a variety of industries and sectors.

In the first two years students will build a foundation in the essentials of effective business management. This foundation prepares students for the options to engage with applied learning within an industry placement, or to explore diverse cultures through studying abroad within the extensive partner network.

This course offers students excellent employability skills including professional presentation, team working, leadership, communication and problem solving.
courses.4n2w:
Program Description

Whilst studying, students will gain a strong foundation in a wide range of business and management disciplines, together with skills and experience that will enable them to meet the challenges of a career in the fast changing international business environment.

Students will become competent in the analysis of the impact of cultural differences on a wide variety of business decisions and consumer behaviour.

The study of the international business environment and its particular needs will be reinforced by a compulsory year abroad of study or a combination of study abroad and work-based learning abroad.
courses.4n36:
With its rich history, abundance of attractions and world-famous festivals, the city is a centre for travellers and tourists from all over the world. Hospitality and tourism businesses flourish here, so students will have plenty of opportunities to gain work experience.

Students will develop their skills in the design, delivery and management of food, beverage and accommodation to top industry standards within a global business environment.

With options of a 24-week work placement, this course will equip students with the knowledge and practical preparation them need to successfully pursue a career in international hospitality management.
courses.4n5p:
With its rich history, abundance of attractions and world-famous festivals, the city is a centre for travellers and tourists from all over the world. Hospitality and tourism businesses flourish here, so students have plenty of opportunities to gain work experience.

This course allows students to pursue a career in both the hospitality and festival and event industries. With international hospitality management at the core, it has been designed to meet the current needs of the industry.

Similar to the BA (Hons) International Hospitality Management, students will study the principles of hospitality management, specialising in festival and event. At ENU, they teach their students in an applied way, which means that they will be able to put their learnings into practice. Students will apply this knowledge to practical situations on an industry-based work placement or live project, preparing them for a career in the hospitality and festival and event industries.

Alternatively students can choose to study abroad through the international exchange links in Europe and the USA.

This course is studied full-time over four years. Students will learn by a variety of teaching methods including lectures, tutorials and independent study. There is a work placement option in Year 3.
courses.8f9f:
The International Foundation Year in Nursing provides a strong foundation for students looking to pursue a career in healthcare.

This programme is designed to help students build the essential academic and English language skills needed to begin their nursing degree at Edinburgh Napier University. It provides a strong foundation in healthcare-related subjects, preparing them for success in both their studies and future professional practice.
courses.7k0q:
The International Stage One (IS1) represents the first year of a four-year undergraduate degree which caters specifically for the needs of international students. It provides an opportunity for students to take part in a bespoke programme which maps against the standard first year offered at Edinburgh Napier University (ENU). They will be able to study in the supportive environment of an international college situated on an ENU campus and follow a Learning, Teaching and Assessment Approach designed to meet their learning needs while still being immersed in a university environment, accessing University facilities and resources and following university undergraduate regulations. Successful completion of the IS1 enables them to join the second year of their undergraduate studies at Edinburgh Napier University.

During students' studies on International Stage One (IS1) they will enhance their English language capabilities, develop academic study skills appropriate to the United Kingdom Higher Education environment and acclimate to living and studying in another country and cultural context very different from their own. Alongside language and study skills tuition, those working on the International Stage One are also able to study content modules within a chosen field of study and which are closely related to modules delivered in Edinburgh Napier University (ENU)’s standard year one. They are therefore able to join their second year studies at Scottish Credit and Qualifications Framework (SCQF) Level 8 alongside continuing students with increased confidence in both their language and study skills and subject knowledge.

The Bachelor of Science (Honours) Applied Microbiology course provides students with specialist skills in food, medical and environmental microbiology and biotechnology while also giving them a broad understanding of the biological sciences.

For students who've finished high school but don’t meet the entry requirements for university, a Foundation Certificate can help them gain entry to an undergraduate degree. After completing this pathway option students qualify for progression to the 1st year of an undergraduate degree at City, University of London.

A student’s course length is determined mainly by their English language level (UKVI IELTS score). Students on all course lengths take a set of common or similar modules to gain a solid base of skills for university. Students taking a course longer than 2 terms, will take additional modules designed to improve one or more of their English language level, academic skills, and basic knowledge of particular subjects.

This LLB Law degree gives students a foundation in the essential skills and knowledge needed to be successful in law and related fields.

It gives students a range of transferable skills which will help if they want to pursue a career path both within and outside law. Students will leave confident in their abilities and equipped with the skills demanded by employers. Students will be trained to deal with challenging situations in the law or law related workplace and demonstrate a high degree of professionalism in their work environment.

The knowledge and intellectual competencies students gain will enable them to develop as a mature, professional individual. This degree is also highly internationalised in its content, delivery and assessment strategies. City aims to produce highly qualified individuals with a global perspective on the law.

Our Accounting & Finance BSc provides a hands on experience of financial study, developing skills to take into any financial career.

Accounting & Finance at King’s College London covers foundations of general management as well as accounting and finance in the first year while offering more specialist content throughout the rest of the degree. The accounting and finance focus becomes more pronounced in the second and third years of the course, where a number of more advanced modules in financial reporting, management accounting, asset management, auditing, corporate finance and taxation will be offered.

There are two things that are unique about studying accounting and finance at King’s: one is the strong grounding in a broad, social science-based approach to learning; the other is a keen emphasis on the way in which financial careers are being reshaped by technological innovation. This dual focus on social science and technological innovation translates into a concern to cultivate accounting and finance graduates that are socially rounded and technologically adept.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).

Study for a BSc Anatomy, Developmental & Human Biology degree at King's College London.

The Anatomy, Developmental & Human Biology BSc degree course offers you an opportunity to explore how the human body is constructed, how anatomical structures function normally and the basis of human diseases caused when these structures do not form properly or become damaged.

You will learn how our anatomy has emerged through the study of evolution, embryonic development, anatomical structure-function relationships and ageing. In doing so, you will consider how human anatomy is constructed and functions normally at the organismal, tissue, cellular and molecular levels.

We are one of only a few UK universities to offer an Anatomy BSc programme. Our students have access to extensive, modern dissection room facilities and the Gordon Museum of Pathology. Our course is research-led, providing an opportunity for you to study human anatomy in depth and to integrate this knowledge with cutting-edge research in anatomy, embryology, evolution, cell and molecular biology. You will learn how these rapidly advancing and interlinked fields of scientific investigation are helping us better understand how the human body works and the origins of many human diseases.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).
courses.pive6f:
Anatomy, Developmental and Human Biology Intercalated BSc online prospectus

The Anatomy, Developmental & Human Biology Intercalated BSc offers students already on medical degree programmes the opportunity to achieve an additional specialist degree in just one year. The programme will help you to develop critical scientific research skills, and gain knowledge of a diverse range of anatomy-related fields. These include applied and clinical anatomy, ageing, regenerative medicine topics, genetics, cell and developmental biology, neuroscience, psychology and behavioural science, which reflect the teaching strengths of the department and wider School of Biosciences.

It offers a wide choice of taught units, including advanced human anatomy, biology of cancer, developmental neurobiology and psychology/behavioral science. You are also required to complete a compulsory research project, either library-based or experimental, on topics that reflect the research strengths and interests of the department.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).

This Ancient History BA allows you to explore a wide range of diverse periods, places and cultures and learn how to work with a range of sources.

You’ll also learn how to work with primary and documentary sources, such as literary texts, and ancient inscriptions. This will help you to engage with the various types of history you’ll encounter, including social, cultural, political, military, economic, and religious history, and to scrutinise current debates in scholarship.

You’ll join the best department for Classics research in the UK (REF 2021), meaning that you’ll be taught by academics at the forefront of their respective fields. And we offer a range of exciting opportunities that include handling sessions in London museums like the British Museum, unique module coverage from the Bronze Age to modern Greece, and the possibility of travel in classical lands.

On this programme, you will have the opportunity to apply to study abroad, supported by the Study Abroad Tutor in your department and King’s Global Mobility Office. Together with partner organisations around the world, you will be supported in navigating your international, educational journey, developing new skills and competences and learning to apply different perspectives to your chosen discipline.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).

This joint honours Artificial Intelligence & Philosophy combines AI with philosophy’s study of the big questions.

Our new joint-honours degree combines Artificial Intelligence with philosophy’s study of the big questions. This unique degree is the first of its kind in the UK, and will equip you with technical and critical thinking skills that open doors to careers in tech, government, journalism, business, research and more.

Students on the Artificial Intelligence & Philosophy with a Year Abroad BSc will spend their third year studying abroad before returning to complete a final year with King’s. Students on the three year course may transfer to the four year Artificial Intelligence & Philosophy with a Year Abroad BSc.

On this programme, you will have the opportunity to apply to study abroad, supported by the Study Abroad Tutor in your department and King’s Global Mobility Office. Together with partner organisations around the world, you will be supported in navigating your international, educational journey, developing new skills and competences and learning to apply different perspectives to your chosen discipline.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).
courses.vc3zhc:
Study Artificial Intelligence BSc at King's College London.

Our BSc in Artificial Intelligence will provide you with a comprehensive and cutting-edge understanding of AI theory and practice. AI significantly affects people’s lives, and it is encountered in more and more of our daily activities. These include activities such as using smart devices, digital voice assistants, and travel aids, as well as banking online or receiving personalised recommendations about movies to rent.

Our programme is structured around AI's core dimensions, including the foundations of AI, data science and Machine Learning. You’ll study reasoning, interactions and autonomous agents including robotics. You'll also gain a deep understanding of the ethics and philosophy of AI and its shifting role in society through exploring the social, legal, and professional dimensions. Throughout your degree, you’ll apply your skillset to tackle complex projects inspired by real-world industry problems. This could include working with an external company on developing a tech solution to an industry problem in your third year.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).

courses.ntxvys:
Study BSc Biochemistry degree at King's College London | How to apply and entry requirements

Biochemistry is the study of the molecular basis of life and our Biochemistry BSc course will introduce you to all areas of modern biochemistry. You will gain the practical knowledge and skills needed to work in a scientific research environment, as well as transferable skills to begin a career in a variety of fields both in science and beyond. The course also features options to study abroad, undertake work placement or extend to a four-year MSci.

Studying a Biomedical Science degree with us means that you will be able to enjoy the flexibility to choose your degree after your first year with our Common Year One curriculum. All Biomedical Science disciplines are covered in the first year, making the decision for your future an informed one.

You will be able to choose from the following Biomedical science degrees; Anatomy, Developmental & Human Biology BSc, Biochemistry BSc, Biomedical Science BSc, Medical Physiology BSc, Molecular Genetics BSc, Neuroscience BSc,and Pharmacology BSc.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).
courses.o37tox:
Study Biomedical Engineering BEng in the Department of Biomedical Engineering at King's College London.

Our Biomedical Engineering BEng course has been designed to train the next generation of biomedical engineers working in healthcare research and development. Upon completion you will go on to specialise in medical engineering, medical physics or apply for further study in Medicine.

The practice of medicine is being transformed by the increasing role of engineering, physics, mathematics and computer science. Our three- year course will position you at the forefront of these developments.

Our Biomedical Engineering BEng degree will provide you with a foundation in mathematics engineering and science, along with a biomedical engineering curriculum.

This course information applies to 2027 entry only. The University may make changes to a programme of study or modules. See full disclaimer in our Terms and Conditions.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).
courses.s5m7fj:
Study BSc Biomedical Science degree in the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine at King's College London.

Our flexible Biomedical Science BSc offers an interdisciplinary undergraduate education in the biosciences that underpin our understanding of human health and the diagnosis and treatment of disease. You will benefit from high-quality teaching in the School of Bioscience Education and choose from a wide range of modules to develop a Biomedical Science degree course that reflects your scientific strengths and interests.

Studying a Biomedical Science degree with us means that you will be able to enjoy the flexibility to choose your degree after your first year with our Common Year One curriculum. All Biomedical Science disciplines are covered in the first year, making the decision for your future an informed one.

You will be able to choose from the following Biomedical science degrees; Anatomy, Developmental & Human Biology BSc, Biochemistry BSc, Biomedical Science BSc, Medical Physiology BSc, Molecular Genetics BSc, Neuroscience BSc, and Pharmacology BSc.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).
courses.riub54:
Our Business Management BSc will provide you with a complete business education.

Business Management at King’s is a broad discipline encompassing a number of specialist fields including economics, psychology, sociology, accounting, finance, marketing, law and human resource management. With strong links to the business world surrounding our campus in the heart of London, our students have excellent networking opportunities and a wealth of entrepreneurial, business and economic societies to engage with and enhance their studies.

During the course you will earn a total of 120 credits for each year of study. In your first year, you will mainly study required modules to ensure a strong and broad foundation from which to pursue your later studies. In the second and third years, there is a further mix of required and optional modules, providing you with the opportunity to explore specific areas or to continue with a broad base of study.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).

courses.s9yms3:
Learn about the various undergraduate study options available at King's.

Browse our A-Z course finder to see a full list of courses offered at King's College London. Most courses enable you to take optional modules in addition to compulsory core modules. Therefore, where your course provides flexibility in module selection, as a student at King's you will be able to tailor your degree to match your interests.

Major/minor honours - at least half of the modules are in the major subject and a quarter in the supporting subject.

King's offers courses at different levels: the application method may be dependent on which one you choose. If you cannot find the type of study you are looking for here, you may be interested in short courses, summer courses or postgraduate courses which are also offered by King's.

See our academic preparation courses pages for more details of our 16, 11 or 6 weeks full-time, intensive courses open to non-native English speaking students who are holding offers to study at King's.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).
courses.1wi1:
Architecture is a profession, and this course is an integral part of a sequence of steps – RIBA parts 1, 2 and 3 - that leads to entry into it. Criteria for entry on to the UK Register of Architects are prescribed by the Architects Registration Board (ARB). The ARB and the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) have agreed to hold the criteria in common and successful completion of this Honours Degree course gives Part 1 exemption. In addition to this, the RIBA has introduced new Themes and Values for Architectural Education, which includes further focus on climate literacy, health and life safety, ethical practice, and research literacy. The modules in the course work within this framework to provide a coherent balance of intellectual and practical skills, as well as facilitating various avenues to develop students' transferable and digital skills for a wide range of employment.

The course sits in the Department of Landscape and Architecture, one of four Departments in the School of Arts, which is one of three Schools (with the Design School and the School of Creative and Cultural Industries) in the Faculty of Kingston School of Art (KSA). It is located in the compact Knights Park campus, where it is directly adjacent to the range of other creative disciplines within KSA. It has immediate access to excellent and wide-ranging resources for physical making, an opportunity which sits at the heart of the pedagogy in each of the programmes and forms a key component of the BA Architecture programme.

Graduates find employment in architectural and multidisciplinary built environment practices. Others find work in environmental, planning consultancies, some in the public sector, and in not-for-profit agencies.
courses.1wi2:
This course prepares students for a career in art direction in the creative industries. Students will develop practical, conceptual and analytical skills in visual communication to create effective advertising and visual identities for organisations and projects.

Students will learn to visualise, collaborate, experiment and project manage as they work on real-world projects with other students and industry professionals. Students will also develop their knowledge of the creative industries, exploring topics such as design thinking, branding and strategy for creative organisations. Students will have creative freedom and be encouraged to undertake non-commercial creative projects.

Students will also have lots of opportunities to work on live projects with creative companies and institutions, as well as being able to work with their classmates in Kingston's student-powered creative agency, Studio KT1.

Throughout the course students will also develop the commercial and organisational skills and understanding needed to work effectively in the creative and cultural sector. This degree prepares students for a career in art direction and advertising in creative enterprises such as fashion and media.
courses.1wi3:
This course prepares students for a career in exhibitions and events in the creative industries. Students will develop practical and analytical skills for the curation, conception, resourcing, marketing and budgeting of an exhibition or event.

Students will learn to visualise, collaborate, experiment and project manage as they work on real-world projects with other students and industry professionals. Students will also develop their knowledge of the creative industries, exploring topics such as design thinking, branding and strategy for creative organisations. Students will have creative freedom and be encouraged to undertake non-commercial creative projects.

The course also offers opportunities to work on live projects with creative companies and institutions, as well as alongside their classmates in Kingston's student-powered creative agency, Studio KT1.

Throughout the course students will also develop the commercial and organisational skills and understanding needed to work effectively in the Creative and Cultural sector.

Kingston School of Art's graduates work in organisations such as the Barbican, Foundling Museum, Hauser & Wirth, National Archives, Open-City, the London Transport Museum and the V&A Museum.
courses.1xrz:
Aerospace engineering at Kingston has an innovative curriculum, excellent links with industry and cutting edge facilities. Kingston is the perfect place to study aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, dynamics and materials.

Students will put theory straight into practice, applying what they learn to the problems of aerospace design and taking part in a group design project.

The course is taught by the Department of Aerospace and Aircraft Engineering. Staff have a wide range of experience across research and industry and continue to practice and research at the cutting edge of their discipline. This ensures that the courses are current and industry informed ensuring they get the most relevant and up-to-date education possible.

The Aerospace Engineering BEng(Hons) course is accredited by the Royal Aeronautical Society for 2018 entry and satisfies, in part, the academic requirements for Chartered Engineer (CEng) registration and in full, Incorporated Engineer (IEng) registration. Renowned companies are involved in course delivery, placements, final year projects and industry talks. Companies range from global leaders KLM Engineering, Marshall Aerospace and the Defence Group, Airbus UK, Astrium Eads, GE Aircraft and Lockheed, to small and medium enterprises such as Aero Optimal, Aircraft Research Associates and Aim Aviation.

Graduates have gained jobs with Boeing, BAE Systems, Qinetiq, Airbus, Rolls-Royce, Thales, General Electric and British Airways. Many graduates go on to study at masters and doctoral level.

This is an ideal degree for anyone considering an engineering career in aviation. It will prepare students to work in aircraft maintenance, airworthiness, aviation management, logistics, systems integration, design, support, manufacturing, and air transport economics. Studies include aerodynamics, propulsion, structures and materials science and the performance of aircraft. Through practical work in laboratories and workshops, students will apply the engineering principles they learn. This degree will also develop career skills such as effective communication, presentation, team-working, planning and project management.

This course aligns with the UK Standard for Professional Engineering Competence (UKSPEC) and meets the academic requirements for Incorporated Engineering (IEng) Membership of the Royal Aeronautical Society (RAes).

The course is taught by the Department of Aerospace and Aircraft Engineering. Staff have a wide range of experience across research and industry and continue to practise and research at the cutting edge of their discipline. This ensures that the courses are current and industry informed ensuring students get the most relevant and up to date education possible. Renowned companies are involved in course delivery, placements, final year projects and industry talks. These companies range from global leaders KLM Engineering, Marshall Aerospace and the Defence Group, Airbus UK, Astrium Eads, GE Aircraft, and Lockheed, to small and medium enterprises such as Aero Optimal, Aircraft Research Associates, and Aim Aviation.

Career opportunities include maintenance and licensed aircraft engineering, certification, quality assurance, logistics, planning, design, technical services, production and control engineering. Employers are often the military, civil aviation and aerospace companies.
courses.6s5m:
Embark on an exciting journey into the dynamic realm of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, enhanced by the power of Artificial Intelligence. This highly sought-after field addresses some of the most pressing challenges facing society today. Students will not only gain the skills and expertise needed to tackle these issues, but they can also make a global impact by shaping a better future.

This innovative course is designed to equip students with the Future Skills to thrive in the fast-paced world of technology. Students will master the art of harnessing artificial intelligence and other cutting-edge technologies to design, develop and implement intelligent electrical and electronic systems. As a result, students will contribute to ground-breaking solutions that positively influence society and pave the way for a brighter tomorrow. This course prepares students for an array of exciting career paths, ensuring they are ready to capture the boundless opportunities offered by the Fourth Industrial Revolution.

Embrace the UN Sustainable Development Goals and actively contribute to a sustainable future for all. This course curriculum is thoughtfully crafted to integrate these goals, empowering students to incorporate them into their professional work and make a meaningful difference. This course caters to the needs of diverse communities and is taught by experienced academics from diverse backgrounds. This unique learning environment allows students to engage with people from different cultures and perspectives, fostering a truly global outlook and enriching their educational experience.
courses.9gi2:
The BSc (Hons) Business Management provides a broad and contemporary business education designed around the organisations and challenges of the future.

Students develop knowledge across management, leadership, people, strategy, enterprise and organisational performance, while building the practical and digital capabilities needed to succeed in a changing economy.

The degree takes a people-centred approach to management. It explores how effective leaders motivate and develop employees, build organisational cultures and respond to complex challenges.

Digital business, artificial intelligence, analytics and innovation are also central to understanding modern organisations. Students consider how technology is changing business models, decision-making, customer relationships and the workplace.

The degree is designed to maintain broad career options while giving students a strong business identity. Whether graduates pursue careers in management, consultancy, operations, entrepreneurship or other commercial fields, they will develop transferable skills that can be applied across a range of sectors.

Business involves more than understanding how individual functions operate. It also requires an understanding of how people, ideas, resources and decisions come together to create organisational performance. The degree provides a broad view of business while allowing students to explore contemporary issues shaping organisations.

Students examine leadership, organisational behaviour, strategy, people management, enterprise, digital business and responsible management. Artificial intelligence and analytics help them understand how technology is influencing decision-making and transforming business models.

Particular emphasis is placed on leadership and people. Successful organisations require managers who can communicate effectively, motivate employees, develop talent and create environments in which individuals and teams can perform successfully.

Responsible leadership is central to effective modern management. Throughout the degree, students explore ethics, responsible decision-making, sustainability and the wider impact of organisational activity.

Students consider how businesses can balance commercial performance with their responsibilities towards employees, customers, communities and the environment. Themes connected to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals help them understand the contribution businesses can make to wider sustainable development.

The course combines a strong Lincolnshire identity with a global outlook. Students explore business challenges, markets and opportunities from local, national and international perspectives.

Lincolnshire’s diverse economy provides opportunities to understand organisations operating across agriculture and food, manufacturing, tourism, retail and professional services. Students also consider global supply chains, international competition, technological change and emerging markets.

The programme develops students’ ability to analyse complex business problems and turn ideas into practical recommendations. It therefore combines academic understanding with applied learning and professional development.
courses.52ck:
With a high level of professional exemptions from the accounting bodies ACCA, ICAEW, CIPFA, AIA and IFA, this challenging course will help students become a qualified accountant or start work in a finance-related career. Students will have access to an extensive network of industry contacts to help with optional work experience placements and projects.

Through this course, students will develop their academic writing, their independent research skills and their practical skills in business and accounting software such as Microsoft Excel, Sage and Oracle. The programme is delivered through a blend of lectures, seminars, workshops, presentations and plenary sessions.

Between them, the staff have accumulated an impressive level of academic and professional experience in public audit, taxation, financial and management accounting, and information systems. Occasionally, distinguished external speakers are invited to make presentations on contemporary accounting, finance and business-related issues.

London Metropolitan University places particular emphasis on employability, and the lecturers, who have a wide network of industry contacts, can help students with optional work experience placements and projects.

On completion of this course, students will receive full exemption from all of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA)’s fundamental exam papers.

An International Bright Futures Scholarship in the amount of £3,000 will automatically be applied to eligible students with overseas fee status starting a degree with London Met in the 2024/25 academic year. This scholarship includes a tuition fee reduction for the duration of students' studies and is applicable to both undergraduate and postgraduate courses.

Tuition Deposit is £4,000 for all students excluding those from Punjab and Haryana for whom the deposit amount will remain at 50%

Designed to equip students for a successful career in marketing communications and public relations, this undergraduate degree explores the drivers and dynamics of the communications industry, covering the key elements of modern theory and practice.

Studying in London means students will be immersed in one of the world's most important centres for advertising, communications and public relations with plenty of opportunities for industry experience. The course is recognised by the Chartered Institute of Public Relations and students will also have the opportunity to apply for accreditation from the Chartered Institute of Marketing.

This career-oriented course explores the contemporary marketing industry, covering the key aspects of modern advertising, marketing communications and public relations. Students will learn techniques and approaches that will help them balance the often conflicting demands of an organisation’s stakeholders, enabling them to deliver clear and consistent results.

An International Bright Futures Scholarship in the amount of £3,000 will automatically be applied to eligible students with overseas fee status starting a degree with London Met in the 2024/25 academic year. This scholarship includes a tuition fee reduction for the duration of students' studies and is applicable to both undergraduate and postgraduate courses.

This degree course offers a multifaceted design-based education that, on successful completion, provides exemption from RIBA 1 – the first stage of a professional qualification in architecture. Typically, graduates go on to RIBA Part 2 and 3 at London Metropolitan University.

London Met's course is centred on three key themes: the idea and practice of making, an architect’s professional duty of care, and social and environmental responsibility.

Students will take classes in the well-resourced design studios, where they’ll have the chance to work with high-end analogue and digital printing facilities. Students will also get access to the textile, ceramic, furniture-making and photography workshops.

London Met complements formal teaching and field work with practical design exploration. The staff is made up of renowned practitioners who bring a wealth of technical expertise to the table and who provide insight into industry best practices within a constantly evolving arena.

An International Bright Futures Scholarship in the amount of £3,000 will automatically be applied to eligible students with overseas fee status starting a degree with London Met in the 2024/25 academic year. This scholarship includes a tuition fee reduction for the duration of students' studies and is applicable to both undergraduate and postgraduate courses.

Tuition Deposit is £4,000 for all students excluding those from Punjab and Haryana for whom the deposit amount will remain at 50%
courses.52e3:
This innovative Business Management degree, designed in conjunction with leading industrialists, provides students with insights and understanding of contemporary business themes including entrepreneurship. The course equips students with vital business skills and provides them with an opportunity to practice them in both traditional and virtual business environments. In addition to the degree, students will gain the highly sought after and widely recognised CMI Level 6 Diploma in Management and Leadership.

The University's Business Management BA is accredited at level 6 by the Chartered Management Institute (CMI), an internationally renowned professional body. While studying on this course, students will gain membership to CMI and will be able to access its facilities, attend events, join a mentoring scheme and access over 220,000 live management job postings.

This course will equip students with the key business skills and knowledge needed to succeed in multinational organisations. Students will be provided with an in-depth understanding of all stages of the business management process, from conceptualisation to strategic evaluation.

Students will study a broad range of fields such as finance management, economics, marketing, strategy and human resources, and get the chance to apply their theoretical knowledge to real-life, up-to-date case studies. Students will also hear from specialist guest lecturers, visit a variety of organisations and participate in online business simulations throughout their course. The University’s business incubator, Accelerator, will prove an invaluable resource for flexing their entrepreneurial muscles. Students will have the option to visit the Accelerator facilities and to participate in sessions and competitions.

Students will also have the opportunity to participate in work-based learning as part of their degree. This will give students real-world experience that will set them apart from other graduates when they enter the job market, as well as giving them the chance to put their newfound knowledge to the test.

On completing the course, students will receive their Business Management BA (Hons) degree and a Level 6 Chartered Management Institute (CMI) diploma.

An International Bright Futures Scholarship in the amount of £3,000 will automatically be applied to eligible students with overseas fee status starting a degree with London Met in the 2024/25 academic year. This scholarship includes a tuition fee reduction for the duration of students' studies and is applicable to both undergraduate and postgraduate courses.

Tuition Deposit is £4,000 for all students excluding those from Punjab and Haryana for whom the deposit amount will remain at 50%
courses.51am:
This four-year Business Management (Foundation Year) BA (Hons) degree has a built-in foundation year (Year 0) that provides students with an alternative route into higher education if they don't have traditional qualifications or can't meet the business management entry requirements.

During the foundation year, students will engage with business challenges in a stimulating environment, while boosting their confidence and acquiring crucial academic skills. This acts as excellent preparation for the subsequent three years of study, which will allow students to specialise in more specific and advanced areas of business.

The innovative Business Management (Foundation Year) BA (Hons) degree has been devised with valuable industry input, giving students an edge when it comes to seeking that all-important job when they graduate.

At London Metropolitan University, students will acquire key business skills and knowledge in the classroom but will be provided with a wide range of opportunities outside of the classroom too. The University is home to Accelerator, which provides advice, support, networks, knowledge and resources that can help students turn a business idea into reality. Based in Shoreditch, Accelerator is a unique resource that has helped many students and graduates establish their own businesses.

Students will share their foundation year with students on other business-related foundation year courses. This allows students to share ideas and insights with their classmates before going on to specialise in their subsequent years of study. Should students decide during their foundation year that they’d like to specialise in a different area of business, there is also some flexibility to allow them to do this.

Following the foundation year, students will study the same course content and get the same choice of modules as those who study the Business Management BA (Hons) course. Here, students will have the opportunity to explore decision-making, leadership, organisation design and management, with a range of optional modules to choose from. Alternatively, students can choose to transfer to the Music Business BA (Hons) course if they'd prefer.

Students will graduate with a full undergraduate degree with the same title and award as those who studied the traditional three-year course, but they will also gain a Level 5 Chartered Management Institute (CMI) diploma. As a member of the CMI, students can access their facilities, attend events and access over 200,000 live management jobs and its mentoring scheme.

An International Bright Futures Scholarship in the amount of £3,000 will automatically be applied to eligible students with overseas fee status starting a degree with London Met in the 2024/25 academic year. This scholarship includes a tuition fee reduction for the duration of students' studies and is applicable to both undergraduate and postgraduate courses.

Tuition Deposit is £4,000 for all students excluding those from Punjab and Haryana for whom the deposit amount will remain at 50%
courses.52e4:
This Business Management and Human Resource Management degree course is perfect if students want to study business but they are also a people person who wants to help others reach their full potential.

Students will learn how to deal with issues and challenges facing the world of business while also developing the skills needed to attract and retain the right people, at the right time. If they want to, students will also have the opportunity to explore employment law.

This Business Management and Human Resource Management BA (Hons) degree focuses on understanding businesses, the business environment and how to manage the people within them.

Human resource management (HRM) is a key driving force for successful businesses. Because London Metropolitan University recognises this element is so important to business strategy, they’ve developed a course that doesn’t just teach students about core business principles, but also incorporates the people side of things too.

In the first year, students will develop a solid foundation of business management principles that they’ll build on in their second and third year. Students will also learn how to apply business theory to practical scenarios and learn how to acquire, motivate, develop and retain talent.

As the business landscape has changed in recent years, more people are needed to work flexibly across roles. This course is designed to educate students on change management and how to embrace this, aiming to make students more employable when they graduate.

An International Bright Futures Scholarship in the amount of £3,000 will automatically be applied to eligible students with overseas fee status starting a degree with London Met in the 2024/25 academic year. London Metropolitan University's Business Management and Marketing BA degree is a joint honours programme that will provide students with expertise in both disciplines, offering them a greater range of career opportunities on graduation. The variety of skills will make a student an attractive contender for developing their management and leadership career.

London Metropolitan University's course is accredited by the Chartered Institute of Marketing (CIM) and students will receive exemption from two out of three units that are necessary to obtain the CIM Certificate in Professional Marketing. This is a highly sought-after qualification in the marketing industry, especially if students are considering a career in marketing management. The professional certificate means students will be rewarded with two qualifications by the time they finish their studies. This would give students a ‘competitive edge’ in the job market.

As well as developing the skills and knowledge required for either a career in business management or as a professional marketer, the business management and marketing course will provide students with entrepreneurial skills and understanding that will allow them to start their own business.

If students are passionate about starting their own business, they will not only gain the necessary academic knowledge and skills on the course, but also receive encouragement and support through the Accelerator. The Accelerator is a business incubator that helps students make their business dreams a reality by offering mentoring, advice and workshops. Accelerator has supported many successful budding entrepreneurs and can support students with developing any business idea they might have. Through the Accelerator, students will also get the opportunity to enter the Big Idea Challenge for a chance to win a share of the £30,000 prize to launch their business.

This programme is uniquely comprehensive among business management and marketing courses in the UK. In addition to learning broad marketing skills that apply to the commercial world, the programme also provides students with opportunities to develop new specialist marketing skills to help improve society through the relatively new field of Social Marketing. In this new field, students will learn how to apply the latest marketing techniques to social problems, such as obesity, drunk-driving, discrimination and domestic violence. Lecturers will introduce the concepts and history of social marketing based on their own innovative research. Completing this module will give students an advantage when competing for jobs in the third and public sector.

As part of the course, students will have the opportunity to undertake short and long accredited work placements. This opportunity may be strengthened with undertaking another of London Metropolitan University's innovative modules that equip students with skills for employment, such as the Theory and Practice of Selling module. As all business professionals know, selling is an essential function of business and on this module, students will develop vital negotiation and selling techniques that will ensure them success in their career. Past students on the module have found that it has helped them gain recognition from the Institute of Sales and Marketing Management (ISMM), a professional organisation that represents sales professionals in the UK.

This business management and marketing programme not only aims to improve students' career opportunities, but also seeks to accelerate their cultural and personal growth. Students will find opportunities to study abroad for a semester in places such as Europe, Japan or the USA, where they will be immersed in a new culture and acquire new perspectives. International students visiting from London Metropolitan University's partner institutions will also expand students' world view and help students appreciate business management and marketing on an international scale.

The innovative Bachelor of Architecture (Honours) in Architecture course aims to nurture creative design leaders who flourish in architectural practice, with first-rate communication and management skills, as well as multidisciplinary knowledge and abilities. It aims to produce exceptional architects through an education that is immersed in hands-on experiences.

Architects are involved in the planning and design of the buildings and spaces people inhabit. Architecture is everywhere and brings together many fields of human endeavor, including art, history, physics, engineering, and more.

The Architecture undergraduate program is an innovative course founded on Loughborough University's 100 years of 'theory and practice' culture to foster learning in both the university and the workplace. The Architecture program will allow students to study with allied courses in the School and wider University to mimic real-life work scenarios. More specifically, the program exploits Loughborough University's internationally-renowned expertise across the built environment disciplines, including construction, engineering, and building energy. A significant part of the program is studio-based, supported by a dedicated team of architectural practitioners.

Every year, Loughborough University holds an End of Year Show to celebrate the year’s achievements and showcase student work to practitioners interested in hiring students and graduates.
courses.21z6:
The Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Accounting and Financial Management course is designed to prepare students for careers in diverse areas of accounting, finance and management and to equip them to deal with the challenges of an ever-changing business world. One of the key goals of the Accounting and Financial Management program is to develop the wider skills and intellectual independence that graduates will need to thrive in a long, rewarding professional career. This course offers students the opportunity to study a much wider range of subjects than those of the narrow professional syllabuses.

The course develops skills valued by employers including independent learning and research, analytical skills, teamwork, presentation skills, project work, computer skills and numeracy. Lectures are supported by online resources, tutorials, workshops, seminars and discussion groups. The wide variety of optional modules allows students to develop specialist skills and tailor their degree to suit their career aspirations.

Skills for employability is a key part of the Loughborough University experience and can really boost students' job prospects and this program has a module specifically built in to help students develop their study and employability skills. There are also specific modules in entrepreneurship to help those with aspirations to start or develop their own businesses.
courses.22bb:
The Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Commercial Management and Quantity Surveying program is linked to real-life construction problems, allowing students to develop important professional skills such as analytical thinking, teamwork, presenting, project management and report writing. These will enable them to pursue a career as a professional Commercial Manager, Quantity Surveyor, or another specialist career path.

To meet the needs of tomorrow’s Commercial Managers and Quantity Surveyors, this course is sponsored by the Loughborough Construction Consortium. These companies offer sponsorship, work placements and graduate jobs for students, and enable practical experience in the form of site visits and guest speakers.

The course has achieved dual accreditation by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) and the Chartered Institution of Civil Engineering Surveyors (CICES).

This course comes with the option to work in industry for a year on an approved placement, leading to a Diploma in Industrial Studies (DIS). Students may be able to study abroad for a year, resulting in an additional Diploma in International Studies.
courses.222m:
In today's business world, being international is a necessity. Loughborough's Bachelor of Science (Honours) in International Business is a modern-day business course which concentrates on the links between the major business functions and their role in the international business context. By covering the key management disciplines from a global perspective, students will be equipped for a successful career in a range of business and management roles. Students also have access to an exclusive set of international business modules, plus the chance to develop their language skills.

In the first year of this program, students will be introduced to the major business functions as well as the financial, economic, organizational and international environments that managers and organizations must operate within. In the second year, students will further their study in the international business context and examine how managerial issues vary around the globe. Students will also have the option to undertake an ‘International Semester’, which is a 6-month study abroad scheme. There is also the opportunity to integrate an International Semester into the second year of study, as well as opportunities for students to enhance their language skills in German, French, Spanish and Mandarin.

In the final year of the program students will have the opportunity to build on their experiences on placement or studying abroad. Students will be able to tailor their degree and choose more advanced optional modules that suit their career ambitions. Among others, these include an exclusive set of international business modules, and a wide range of options in management, finance, marketing, operations, analytics, human resource management, and new business development.

Skills for employability is a key part of the Loughborough University's experience and can really boost students' job prospects and this degree has a module specifically built in to help students develop their study and employability skills. There are also specific modules in entrepreneurship to help those with aspirations to start or develop their own businesses.
courses.222u:
The Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Marketing and Management combines a rigorous in-depth knowledge of marketing, together with a solid grounding in business and management to prepare students for a wide range of exciting and rewarding career opportunities. Students will develop highly prized specialist skills in digital marketing, consumer behavior and global brand management, plus essential business and management skills in areas such strategy and leadership.

In the first year of the program, students will build a firm foundation for modules in subsequent years by studying core business and management subjects. In the second year, students will start to develop an in-depth understanding of marketing by attending specialized modules such as marketing research, consumer behavior, global brand management, and digital marketing. They will also be able to choose from a wider range of business options. For those with interest in retailing careers, Loughborough University’s renowned expertise and corporate connections in these areas means we offer a stream of retailing modules that enable students to tailor their degree to suit their career ambitions. Following the professional placement or study abroad year, the final year provides advanced specialized core modules on marketing strategy and planning, and marketing communications, along with a broad range of optional modules in many areas of marketing and management.

The program will also help students to develop their communication and interpersonal skills and their ability to work in groups, essential for working in fast-paced marketing and management roles. Skills for employability is a key part of the Loughborough University experience and can really boost students' job prospects. This program has two modules specifically built in to help them develop their study and employability skills. There are also specific modules in entrepreneurship to help those with aspirations to start or develop their own businesses.
courses.223j:

Students will acquire a thorough understanding of both historical and contemporary developments across a number of key media sectors including the press, broadcasting, film, advertising and digital media.

On the Media and Communication degree, students will gain a wide range of specialist analytical and practical skills relevant to many jobs that involve working with the media and communication industries. The broad scope of the course is designed to enable students to work in a range of different fields of communication and media, and adapt flexibly to a rapidly changing environment where critical understanding and analytical skills are of key importance.
