courses.1oxc:
Program Description

MArch Architecture (ARB / RIBA Part 2) is a two-year full-time course that produces graduate architects who are fully equipped for a career in the architectural profession. It is designed to be the next step for professionals pursuing an accredited pathway to becoming a registered architect.

Fully accredited by the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) and prescribed by the Architects Registration Board (ARB) for the purpose of entry onto the UK Register of Architects, this course satisfies the educational requirements for RIBA Part 2 before moving on to practical experience and Part 3 qualification.

With a focus on educating students with a global outlook, Nottingham Trent University has set collaborative, industry-facing projects set in local, national, and international contexts. The course framework enables students to advance their ability to research, analyse, self-appraise, think critically, work in a team and provide constructive feedback. With core legal, management and design leadership skills built into the course content, students will develop high-level skills needed for advanced industry practice.

Nottingham Trent University's MArch Architecture course content is focused on four core strands: developing design and communication skills; extending student awareness and knowledge of the theory and socio-economic, historic and cultural factors affecting architectural design; advancing student appreciation of technology and construction methods; and developing student knowledge of management, practise and law.

Together, this framework will build upon the skills and knowledge students have already gained, extending their ability to research, analyse, self-appraise, think critically, work in a team and provide constructive feedback.
courses.1osi:
Program Description

The general aim of the course is to produce graduates who are autonomous, able to carry out ethical research studies in different educational contexts, and who can recognised the importance of the application of education theories and research to understand education debates and policies across a range of educational settings and contexts.

This course is designed for a wide range of people interested in education, such as those who currently, or are wanting to, work in an education setting or education policy or research contexts. These education settings range from early years to higher education and all sectors in between and beyond formal education. Therefore the course is designed to provide different modes and routes that are suited to the breadth of potential students who have a range of expertise and experience. As such it has a generic approach to the modules which can then be applied locally and in different contexts.

This is a demanding and exciting research-based programme. It requires students to immerse themselves in reading, thinking, discussion, reflection and writing, enabling them to take the next, critical step in their professional learning.

The degree allows students to investigate a range of issues impacting on education in general and their own field in particular. Nottingham Trent University wants students to challenge their thinking.
courses.1oyf:
Program Description

International security is a complex and rapidly evolving concern for many organisations, institutions and governments. From global climate emergency to the increased threats from terrorist groups, the risks these treats pose to many long-established security policies have led to a rapid development in the field of Security Studies.

Nottingham Trent University's innovative new MA International Relations and Security Studies course gives students a critical approach to complex security problems and enables students to understand them at a global level of analysis. The course offers students the chance develop an in-depth knowledge of security policies their challenges and the interconnected nature of threats.
courses.6xr0:
Embark on an exciting journey with the MA Journalism course. This immersive course offers a perfect blend of hands-on training and academic depth, ensuring students are well-prepared for a thriving career in journalism.

Led by seasoned media professionals, Nottingham Trent University's curriculum covers the entire spectrum of modern journalism, from newsgathering to video editing and harnessing the power of social media. Students will also delve into crucial subjects like media law and politics while having the freedom to personalize their learning journey.

One standout feature of the course is its strong emphasis on social justice journalism, where students will tackle pressing issues on a public-facing platform, making a real impact locally and globally.

Through real-world placements, Newsdays, and collaborative editorial work, students will gain invaluable industry experience, allowing them to follow in the footsteps of NTU's successful journalism graduates.
courses.1owz:
Program Description

This course will equip students with the all-round skills and knowledge needed to build a career as a journalist in magazines, whilst providing them with a deep understanding of the wider publishing business. First and foremost, students will learn how to write, whether it’s an in-depth interview, a sharp news story, a daily blog or a snappy photo caption.

Students will learn how to report, research, interview and edit news stories and features. Using Adobe InDesign, students will develop an understanding of how to plan a page with text, photographs and graphics, sub-edit copy, and write a compelling headline.

Students will get to grips with mobile journalism, using a phone or tablet to record video and audio, and learn how to edit their material into packages. On newsdays and newsweeks, students will produce websites and magazines, working with WordPress, the storytelling platform Shorthand.com, InDesign and Photoshop, as well as creating content for Facebook, Twitter and Instagram.

Students will also examine the business side of magazines and have the chance to pitch their own idea for a new title to a panel of industry professionals.

To underpin their journalism practice, students will gain a solid grounding in media law, public administration and ethics and regulation. Students will also have the opportunity to develop shorthand skills to the NCTJ standard.
courses.85ri: The Master of Arts in Education offers educators and education professionals the opportunity to deepen their understanding of educational theories, policies, and practices. The program covers areas such as curriculum design, pedagogical strategies, educational leadership, and research methodologies. Emphasizing critical reflection and evidence-based practice, graduates are prepared to contribute to the improvement of educational outcomes in various settings.
courses.85sf: The Master of Public Health is an interdisciplinary program focused on improving health outcomes and reducing health disparities. It covers epidemiology, health promotion, global health policy, and healthcare management. Students engage with real-world public health challenges, developing skills in research, critical analysis, and evidence-based intervention. Graduates are prepared for leadership roles in public health agencies, NGOs, and health services.
courses.85sq: The Master of Science in Accounting and Finance equips students with a thorough understanding of financial analysis, corporate reporting, auditing, and investment management. The curriculum integrates theoretical knowledge with practical case studies and simulations, preparing students for roles in financial institutions, accounting firms, or corporate finance departments. It also supports professional development by aligning with globally recognized accounting bodies like ACCA or CIMA.
courses.85sr: The Master of Science in Advanced Computer Science is designed for students who want to deepen their understanding of complex computing systems and technologies. It covers areas such as artificial intelligence, software engineering, and cybersecurity while offering opportunities for hands-on project work and research. The program provides a strong theoretical foundation alongside practical application, preparing graduates for high-level technical careers or doctoral study in computing disciplines.
courses.85su: The Master of Science in Applied Sport and Exercise Nutrition provides a scientific foundation in nutritional principles tailored to athletic performance and physical activity. Students learn how nutrition impacts metabolism, recovery, body composition, and overall athletic performance. The program incorporates both theoretical knowledge and applied practice, preparing graduates to work with sports teams, fitness professionals, or in clinical settings, with the ability to design tailored nutritional plans for a range of physical performance goals.
courses.5e93:
Ravensbourne University London's Design Communication master's degree will enable you to produce industry-quality graphic design, marketing, social media and digital technology assets.

In this exciting new MA Design Communication course, students will gain the knowledge, confidence and professional acumen to creatively position services, systems and need-driven design products.

Students will respond to societal and user needs to expand their graphic communication design skills. Students will be immersed in the tools and processes of digital design and emerging technologies, whilst exploring the value of design thinking and services in a bustling marketplace.

During the course, students will establish a critical design practice, create dynamic interacting spaces, and apply design to respond to a range of needs. Students will engage their target audiences by synthesising creativity with sound business theories – an essential skill that will boost their employability across many potential career avenues.

After studying for the MA Design Communication course, students will have:

  • The hands-on design thinking skills to turn creative visions into truly engaging assets
  • The business and commercial acumen to reach and inspire audiences across all business, international and not-for-profit sectors
  • The confidence to generate real change and influence decision making at the most senior levels
courses.68yk: This MA Design Management course offers a range of interdisciplinary perspectives from business, technology, social enterprises and new venture creation. It offers practical research and work-based projects in all areas shaping the creative economy and the fourth industrial revolution – including the role of creative interventions in technology-enabled business transformation, change management and design leadership.
courses.6fdy:
On this MA/MFA Digital Photography course in London, UK, students will look at image making as a modern platform for communication and explore the role that technology plays in shaping the industry, both in the present and future.

Students will examine relevant media platforms and formats to explore the dissemination and distribution of the digital image.

Students' work will integrate traditional lens-based practices with the contemporary, delving into the likes of computational photography, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and augmented reality (AR). Students will develop and enhance their skills within a series of diverse projects that run through the course. The variety of the modules will enable students to work within a commercial environment, utilise recognised strategies and workflows and create a body of work that showcases the breadth of their ability and potential.

The course benefits from the university's strong industry reputation and places an emphasis on innovation. It will enable students to develop a more independent approach to study and to gain a greater understanding of the industry and the various career pathways within it. Students will be part of a diverse community of creatives, working collaboratively to explore new professional practices. Ravensbourne has strong industry links with a range of high-profile companies, this has previously included the likes of: Apple, Barclays, the BBC, European Space Agency, Marks & Spencer, Museum of London, the Royal Shakespeare Company, Samsung and many more.
courses.6du2: This course allows student to develop the skills for innovative digital platforms, creating avatars and clothing and building the virtual environments in which these interactions will take place. With this the student will develop the advanced knowledge to create and implement complex designs and technology projects. Student will explore systems and platforms for communication, responsive content creation, visualisation, and learn experimental approaches to tackle your work. The student will investigate and realise radical project proposals through collaborative interactions with both peers and industry, and explore the latest advancements in technologies such as AI, Web3, digital fashion, metaverse asset realisation, AR, VR and XR.
courses.25ke:
Throughout the MA Illustration course in London, students will explore the roles of illustration today and its wide-ranging professional applications moving forward. They will experiment across narrative and storytelling methods, which will enable them to present and reposition information in a strategic, accessible and engaging fashion.

Students will examine complex knowledge, data and information and bring it to life with empathy, which will free them to tell stories that need to be told and ensure that no message is lost in translation.

Students can join the new MA Illustration course in Ravensbourne University London's new flagship building, The Institute for Creativity and Technology, where creative minds prosper. By taking on consultancy and organizational roles, as well as developing their own illustration practice, this master's program is designed to make them truly industry ready.
courses.7ak5:
The programme is designed to enable students to specialise in International Business Law, equipping them with a comprehensive and critical understanding of the legal processes governing international business transactions. It covers key areas such as trade law, corporate governance, employment law, and international alternative dispute resolution, while also deepening knowledge of law as an academic discipline. Students develop an understanding of legal methods, concepts, and the broader social, political, and theoretical contexts in which legal systems operate.

The course enhances professional development by broadening students’ perspectives and strengthening their ability to analyse complex legal, economic, cultural, ethical, and political issues in a transnational context. It fosters advanced research and writing skills applicable across a wide range of sectors, including legal practice, policymaking, corporate environments, government, and academia. Students are trained to apply their knowledge creatively and systematically to address challenges in global trade and corporate governance, while building high-level transferable skills, critical self-awareness, and effective problem-solving and decision-making abilities.

A distinctive feature of the programme is its international focus, allowing students to develop advanced expertise in International Business Law alongside strategies for personal and professional growth. Teaching is delivered by experienced academic and industry professionals with strong links to public, private, and enterprise sectors. Students have the opportunity to undertake a traditional dissertation to further develop subject expertise, as well as attend guest lectures from leading specialists, providing valuable insight into contemporary professional practice. Employability skills are embedded throughout the curriculum to align with current industry demands.

Upon completion, graduates demonstrate a systematic understanding of key principles, practices, and emerging issues in International Business Law, as well as the employability skills required for career progression. They gain knowledge of the historical and ongoing influence of English law, the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (CISG), and the regulatory framework of the World Trade Organization (WTO). Students also develop an understanding of the effectiveness and impact of legal mechanisms governing international trade, commercial transactions, and dispute resolution, alongside awareness of the ethical, social, and cultural contexts in which law operates.

The programme also develops advanced cognitive and intellectual skills, enabling students to critically analyse complex legal issues and apply sound judgement in evaluating contractual and trade mechanisms. Graduates are able to assess competing legal arguments, identify potential disputes, and interpret decisions from courts, arbitral bodies, and international organisations. They demonstrate critical awareness of the relationships between international, regional, and domestic legal frameworks, as well as the ability to conduct independent research with originality and authority. The programme culminates in the development of sophisticated analytical, evaluative, and innovative capabilities at Master’s level.
courses.7ak3:
The MSc International Management Degree is designed to help aspiring managers prepare for employment in a wide range of careers and offers enthralling insight into global business perspectives. The course is ideal for individuals seeking to obtain roles within Global, Public and Private Sector Companies.

The course offers a comprehensive overview of global management theories and practices and the opportunity to gain an in depth understanding of the different national and cultural contexts in which firms operate, whilst developing and enhancing analytical and research skills. The course includes a range of relevant subject areas in corporate strategy, international human resource management, sustainability, business innovation as well as finance and accounting that is aimed at developing the necessary knowledge, management and decision making skills that can be applied to international settings. The breadth of topics, combined with an international perspective, prepares students for a variety of roles in an increasingly globalised job market. Being intellectually stimulating and challenging, the course opens up career development opportunities as well as the opportunity to enhance their knowledge and career prospects in areas of further study. The Masters Degree in International Management will give graduates the opportunity to explore a global career in management and to work with International Organizations. This course is designed to prepare students for a variety of management roles across a range of sectors and variety of organisations. This may be within the private, public or voluntary sector, or a multinational company or SME.
courses.7akf:
MSc Social Care, Health and Wellbeing degree offers an excellent opportunity to gain an advanced understanding of the health and social care sector, as well as areas such as equality, diversity, and collaboration. This MSc Social Care, Health and Wellbeing degree will give students an advanced awareness and understanding of the health and social care sector and the challenges that it faces. Specialist modules will broaden students' understanding of key areas such as equality and diversity, integration, and collaboration. Students will also develop enhanced critical and evaluative awareness of the current and emerging issues within health and social care practice.

Students who have qualified, they will have gained specific academic knowledge and practical skills that can be applied in their existing or future career. Alongside this, the college will help students build lifelong learning skills that they can reflect on, articulate, and translate into everyday life. The MSc in Social Care, Health and Wellbeing is well recognised qualification that provides the opportunity to develop students' knowledge for an existing role, improve their prospects, or make a career change. It can also be a first step towards an academic career. This qualification can take students into many different fields – both in the UK and abroad – including multi-agency teams, health promotion projects, refugee and asylum services, hospitals, sheltered accommodation, hospices, day centres, and residential care units. Graduates of this programme may also choose to progress to study at doctorate-level in health and social care, or a related field.
courses.7akc:
Gain a deeper understanding of advanced software methodologies with the MSc Software Engineering degree. Students will be able to analyse advanced software development and recognise resources required for Software Engineering once they have graduated. Jobs directly related to a Software Engineering degree include games, systems and web development, search engine optimization, information systems management, web design and business analysis. This degree also ensures that students can have access and exposure to the latest techniques alongside practical skills.

After graduating with an MSc Software Engineering Degree, students will have stimulated their levels of creative thinking and enhanced their problem solving and decision-making techniques; allowing students to impress employers and make their mark within the industry. This course also paves the way for PhD research studies in software engineering and computing-related subjects. A few roles that students may choose to explore upon graduating with an MSc in Software Engineering are:

  • Applications developer
  • Cyber security analyst
  • Game developer
  • Information systems manager
  • IT consultant
  • Multimedia programmer
  • Web developer
  • Web designer
  • Software engineer
courses.2apa:
This tailormade course has been designed to help students build an international career in a dynamic business environment.

Students will expand their international business career by learning to analyse data, make difficult decisions and implement new strategies in fast-paced, international environments – with practical exercises exposing them to real-life business issues, training them to respond effectively in complex global organisations.

Students will gain a solid understanding of how international business thrive, as well as their problems, drivers of change and cultural dynamics – while building on their knowledge of disciplines including strategic management, finance, marketing and entrepreneurship.

Students will also develop the strategic expertise and creative communication skills needed to succeed in an ever-changing global marketplace, and learn a business-critical language to improve their skills in operating across cultures in international settings.

In the final term, students will either complete a major business project or a written dissertation – researching, analysing and applying their knowledge to a real business case.
courses.2api:
Program Description

This course combines traditional media studies with new practices emerging in the 21st century – teaching students how to innovate, anticipate, analyse and utilise communications across a variety of media platforms.

Students will cover a range of traditional and modern communicative practices across the arts, sciences, humanities, business and industry – exploring how the field is shaped by digital advances. This interdisciplinary approach will give students a thorough grounding in media and communications: as an academic field, a cultural landscape and a complex network of industries.

Examining theories, students will discover the powerful influence media and communications can have socially, culturally and politically – gaining a critical understanding of media and transmedia creation and consumption. Looking at current global issues, students will develop the skills to monitor and analyse audience perceptions and interactions, and implement creative strategies to overcome challenges – using emerging tools and methods like data scraping and data visualisation.

Students will choose from a variety of electives to tailor their studies to topics that interest them – from transmedia storytelling to media regulations, social media marketing, creative economies and even human connection – exploring how dating apps use algorithms to shape matches.

In the final term, students will complete a dissertation, creative project or industry placement – consolidating their learning and gaining insights into one of the most progressive and exciting industries in the world.
courses.640q:
The world of finance was one of the first to adopt today's advances in technology. On this course, students will master the skills needed to work with complex and dynamic financial markets – utilising integrated financial technology and responding to change at pace.

Students will learn to analyse the financial technology (fintech) and innovation sector, explore the digital investment space (including crowd sourcing and crowd funding) and examine new technological disruptions that aim to make financial services more accessible and efficient, personal and secure – including AI, cryptocurrency, cognitive computing, big data and blockchain.

Students will become skilled at analysing new data and connectivity, evaluating technological intelligence and managing risks and uncertainty.

Classes are designed to simulate a real-life experience of the financial industry. Students will benefit from hands-on training in economics software (with access to Thomson Reuters Eikon Terminals, Bloomberg L.P Terminals, Datastream databases and trading rooms on campus), as well as the chance to collaborate with students from all over the world to gain a global insight.

Studying in London, students will have access to financial networks, banking organisations and high-net-worth clients, as well as workshops and industry speakers – exposing them to new insights.

Students will become a financial player with the skills to innovate, analyse new technology and evaluate risks – making financial services more efficient and secure. Students will understand the wider financial industry (from corporate finance to investments) and work across international markets.

This course is also accredited by the Chartered Management Institute (CMI) and, upon completion, students will receive a Level 7 Diploma in Strategic Management and Leadership Practice alongside their degree.
courses.70ob:
The MSc Digital Marketing with Data Analytics offers a comprehensive blend of marketing and analytical skills, preparing students for the dynamic and evolving field of digital marketing.

This programme integrates theoretical knowledge with practical applications, ensuring graduates are well-equipped for the digital marketing landscape. Students will learn how data can help inform decisions in a digital business environment while being mindful of social responsibility, sustainability and business ethics.

Student will gain the knowledge and skills to plan strategically and implement digital marketing campaigns,master a range of data analysis techniques and their application to real life digital marketing decisions.

Develop the marketing skills needed to operate different channels and strategies used in digital marketing, such as search engine optimisation (SEO), gain an ability to apply the techniques and tools utilised within marketing for financial analysis and control.

Student will also gain the knowledge and skills to enter a range of roles in digital marketing including strategic marketing, data analysis for marketing, consumer engagement, marketing communication, and international marketing.
courses.66yt:
Top reasons to study this programme

  • Gain a thorough grounding in strategic business management combined with knowledge of real-life application
  • Ideal for students who are non-native English speakers with a course in Advanced English for Business Studies, also highly relevant for students who are English speakers
  • Opportunity for students to flourish in a supportive learning environment with high-contact teaching approach which is both stimulating and interactive
  • Learn from faculty who have global industry experience as well as guest speakers who share their insights on business management with students
  • Available to study full-time over 16 months, this four-semester programme offers an extended learning opportunity
  • Optional internships provide practical industry experience and enhance career options on graduation
courses.70oc:
MSc Project Management for Sustainability is a pioneering programme designed for the new era of sustainable development in businesses, charities and NGOs (non-governmental organisations). This master’s programme seamlessly combines the principles of sustainability with the rigour of project management, preparing graduates to lead with a unique blend of environmental awareness and practical management skills.

Student will also be offered the opportunity to gain an internationally recognised industry qualification, PRINCE2.7® Foundation and PRINCE2.7® Practitioner.

PRINCE2 is a process-based method for effective project management, and will give students the fundamental skills they need to become a successful project manager. It stands for PRojects IN Controlled Environments, and is used and recognised all over the world.

On this MSc programme student will explore the principles and practice of project management and discover the influence of successful project management on any organisation, with a particular emphasis on improving organisational sustainability.

With the growing recognition of sustainability as a core organisation practice, there’s no better time to study a master’s project management degree with sustainability at its heart.
courses.4v9r:
This course combines a thorough knowledge of business practices and the management of projects with a detailed understanding of specific management practices within the media industries. Students' knowledge of media management will span traditional and digital media and cover how to manage all levels of project, along with digital and marketing skills essential to navigating the wider media landscape encompassing a variety of business models and audiences.

There will be a number of high-calibre tutors leading this course, many of whom are actively producing for TV and big-screen, as well as publishing extensively in the area of media and communications. Students will also benefit from visits by many industry speakers and guest lecturers throughout the year.

  • This course teaches the project management, business and vocational skills essential for working within the media industry and overseeing the life cycle of complex projects from conception to completion
  • This programme believes that learning both creative and business skills is the most effective way to prepare next generation media graduates for the industry
  • The multi- faceted nature of the media demands a multi-skilled professional and that is what Royal Holloway hopes the students will grow into through their experience on this programme.
courses.4vbh:
Program Description

This course will develop your understanding of the theory and practice of accounting and financial management, regardless of your undergraduate background. You will study financial accounting, management accounting, financial management and other important topics in accounting and finance. The course draws upon the extensive research, practical knowledge, and teaching expertise of our accounting and finance academics.

The MSc in Accounting and Financial Management is suitable if:

  • you have an academic background in accounting, finance, business or management and wish to advance your knowledge in accounting and financial management.
  • you have graduated from another discipline, whether arts, sciences or social sciences, and wish to obtain a postgraduate qualification which will provide you with an understanding of accounting and financial management issues.

On graduating you will have acquired a number of transferable skills, including the ability to assess and employ a variety of analytical techniques, write reports, give presentations and work as a team.

  • Strong career prospects in accounting, finance and commercial areas; organisations value graduates with knowledge and understanding of contemporary accounting and financial management who can also reflect on their broader setting and implications.
  • Outstanding research; Royal Holloway sits in the top 25 per cent of UK universities for research which is rated as ‘world-leading’ and ‘internationally excellent’
  • Inspiring international community; 60% of our Management students come from overseas and the 8,500 students at Royal Holloway, University of London are from 130 countries.
courses.4vb5:
Program Description

This course, offered by the Department of Computer Science and the Department of Economics, allows you to specialise in modern quantitative finance and computational methods for financial modelling, which are demanded for jobs in asset structuring, product pricing as well as risk management.

Skills that you will acquire include the ability to:

  • analyse, critically evaluate, and apply methods of computational finance to practical problems, including pricing of derivatives and risk assessment
  • analyse and critically evaluate methods and general principles of computational finance and their applicability to specific problems
  • work with methods and techniques such as clustering, regression, support vector machines, boosting, decision trees, and neural networks
  • analyse and critically evaluate applicability of machine learning algorithms to problems in finance
  • implement methods of computational finance and machine learning using object-oriented programming languages and modern data management systems
  • work with software packages such as MATLAB and R
  • work with Relational Database Systems and SQL

You will be taught by world-leading academics. Research in Machine Learning at Royal Holloway started in the 1990’s, at which time Vladimir Vapnik and Alexey Chervonenkis (the inventors of Support Vector Machines) were both professors here. We have developed both fundamental theory and practical algorithms that have fed into the analytics methods and techniques that are in use today. Current researchers include Alexander Gammerman and Vladimir Vovk – the inventors of conformal predictors theory, a radically new method of estimating the accuracy of each prediction as it is made – and Chris Watkins, originator of reinforcement learning who developed ‘Q-learning’, a work that is fundamental to planning and control.

courses.4vax:
Program Description

The importance of Big Data grows year on year, with sectors including healthcare, manufacturing, retail, administration and others reliant on the insights that accurate data capture and analysis can provide. Study Data Science and Analytics with a Year in Industry at Royal Holloway, University of London and students will develop the practical skills needed to handle and analyse data in a wide variety of fields, preparing them for a rewarding career in Big Data.

This flexible programme gives students the chance to tailor their learning to their own strengths and interests, with a broad range of optional modules including Online Machine Learning, Methods of Bioinformatics and Microeconometrics providing academic scope and variety. Students will be well-equipped to continue their studies at PhD level, which will place them in a strong position to pursue more advanced, research-based roles upon graduation.

Skills that students will acquire include the ability to:

  • work with methods and techniques such as clustering, regression, support vector machines, boosting, decision trees, and neural networks
  • work with structured, unstructured, and time-series data
  • work with software packages such as MATLAB and R
  • design data processing solutions for data-intensive analytics problems
  • work with modern tools for massively distributed data processing, such as Hadoop and Pig, and Cloud Computing tools such as Amazon S3, EC2 and Elastic MapReduce
  • design Extract-Transfer-Load (ETL) pipelines
  • design Data Warehousing and Decision Support System (DSS) solutions
  • work with highly-scalable data-storage solutions, such as MongoDB, Cassandra, HBase, and other NoSQL Data Stores
  • work with data-intensive computing technologies, such as Hadoop MapReduce, Spark, Hive, and Pig
  • work with Cloud Computing tools, such as Amazon S3, EC2 and Elastic MapReduce

Students are encouraged to follow their passion for Data Science and Analytics at Royal Holloway and they will graduate with a desirable Masters degree from a highly regarded department, as well as transferable skillset that’s both in short supply and in high demand by employers. Royal Holloway's location near the M4 corridor – also known as ‘England’s Silicon Valley’ – means students can develop their skills and experience with a year in industry at some of the country's leading technology institutions.

  • By electing to spend a year in business, students will also be able to integrate theory and practice and gain real business experience. In the past, students have secured placements in blue-chip companies such as Centrica, Data Reply, Disney, IMS Health, Rolls Royce, Shell, Sociéte Générale, VMWare and UBS, among others.
  • Benefit from strong industry ties, with close proximity to ‘England’s Silicon Valley’.
  • Graduate with a Master's degree leading to excellent graduate employability prospects.
  • Tailor their learning with a wide range of engaging optional modules.

As an Master of Science Data Science student students will explore how to efficiently find patterns in these vast streams of data. Many research areas have tackled parts of this problem. Machine learning focuses on finding patterns and making predictions from data; ideas from algorithms and databases are required to build systems that scale to big data streams; and separate research areas have grown around different types of unstructured data such as text, images, sensor data, video, and speech.

courses.5zsr:
Policy making is becoming an increasingly complex process in the 21st Century. The context in which we make policy is radically changing, alongside the nature of the issues policymakers are required to address.

Traditional models of policy making are facing challenges from below, through the drive to devolution, and from above, as supra national forms of governance continue to evolve. Alongside, these developments, social issues, such as pollution, crime, and migration, increasingly transcend national boundaries, to present further challenges to policy makers.

This exciting programme seeks to understand the ways that policy is formulated within this evolving and dynamic context, by drawing on the core concepts of policy analysis and theories of policy change. It will offer insights into the policy actors, coalitions and forms of evidence, that shape the creation of both ‘good’ and ‘bad’ policy, as well as providing a detailed understanding of the policy making architecture that characterises local, regional and supranational institutions. Moreover, the programme will explore the social, political, economic and historic contexts in which policy is formulated and the ways that power influences policy formulation.

As well as considering theories of the policy process, the programme offers the opportunity to study across a range of global policy issues and social problems, such as poverty, migration, crime, and homelessness, to understand these theories in action.

Through a suite of module options students can tailor the curriculum to match their interests and career plans. For those students interested in gaining experience in the workplace, we have pathways that incorporate a placement module.

  • development and operation of international and regional institutions
  • past and present transnational challenges in international and regional diplomacy
  • contemporary global challenges such as environmental degradation, trafficking/crime and migration

Students will have the opportunity to take specialist pathways, including specialising in selected regions (Europe, Africa, MENA, Asia, or Latin America and the Caribbean), with opportunities for selected study visits, or take thematic specialisms including international governance, modern diplomacy, security studies, or political violence and terrorism.

Do you want to spend a year studying in a stimulating academic environment, working with staff who are at the forefront of their field and with students from all over the world?

Are you looking for a challenging learning experience, solving real-world problems, addressing complex ethical dilemmas, undertaking independent research projects, and practicing advanced skills for conflict engagement?

Would you like to build a portfolio of work that demonstrates your achievement of a set of professional competencies relevant to employment in the peace, conflict and development fields?

The MA Advanced Practice in Peacebuilding and Conflict Resolution is offered by the internationally recognised Department of Peace Studies and International Development, drawing on over 40 years of experience as a leading centre of peace research and education.

The programme will develop your understanding of the causes and dynamics of social conflict, with a strong focus on case-study analysis. It will allow you to develop informed judgements about when and how to engage constructively with conflict, recognising the strengths and limitations of different approaches to intervention. And you will consider critical questions surrounding and problematising efforts to build peace in different contexts, and in the light of contemporary trends, including converging environmental, economic and political developments.

Whatever their choice, students' studies will examine key contemporary issues such as developments in information technology, free trade and trade protectionism, Brexit, and sustainability.

Natural Resources form the bedrock of global economic development. However, development and use of natural resources have implications for the environment, often leading to other socio-economic and political challenges such as poverty, disease and conflicts, especially in developing countries. The resulting environmental impacts such as climate change, pollution and degradation of habitats and species extinction has also raised serious challenges for governance and diplomacy at the international level, often pitting international economic policies and frameworks with natural resources and environmental governance.

This course will provide you with an excellent understanding of the law and policy issues in this area, and skills necessary to pursue a career in this exciting field, whether this be in private legal practice, as in-house lawyers in corporations, policy-oriented work in intergovernmental and other international institutions in advocacy in civil society organisations.

The course offers a wide range of modules that are contemporary, academically rigorous and skills oriented. The design ensures you gain core knowledge of the wider context framing law and policy in this field whilst giving you the flexibility to tailor your degree to suit your particular interests by choosing from a range of specialist modules. You will explore emerging issues such as a low carbon economy, unconventional and alternative energy, the regulation and governance of multinational corporations and the responsibility of states in addressing these concerns.

The programme will provide students with an applied understanding of Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics. This programme is suitable for applicants from all backgrounds and no prior technical knowledge is required. Students will develop the relevant technical skills they need as part of the programme.

The technical skills students will develop include a knowledge of Python, R, Julia, Weka, AWS, MS Azure, SAS, SPSS, and Excel. Non-technical soft skills, the development of which are key to long-term success in any industry, include data-driven decision-making, critical thinking, business acumen and entrepreneurship, and communication, teamwork and leadership skills.

Students will have the opportunity for a three-month industry placement as part of the programme, giving them invaluable real-world experience and an opportunity to build industry contacts.

The three-month industry placement is not guaranteed; however, students will work closely with a dedicated employer and placement services adviser, who will support students in finding a placement, support students with CV writing and help students apply for roles.

Students will graduate as a confident, creative, enterprising, independent data modeller and interpreter, able to select appropriate AI and DS tools for a given practical problem and perform empirical analysis that feeds into data-driven decision-making.

The future urban environments are being shaped by the design of buildings, larger developments, and landscapes. The student will work across the disciplines of architecture, art, and cultural geography, combining critical debate and artistic practice to aid their development as a designer of physical settings.

The course is highly experimental, aiming to stretch the imagination and critical ability of the individual. They will engage with research on the analysis of city spaces and explore the current issues of global urbanism. Leading their own projects, they will speculate on how urban environments will evolve and graduate with a significant portfolio of work.

In the vibrant backdrop of Brighton, a supportive studio environment and diverse workshops and seminars taught by architects and urban designers are offered.
courses.4qck:
The Sports Journalism course offers vital multi-platform and multimedia skills, along with exclusive connections to Arsenal FC and Brighton & Hove Albion FC.

The program is designed for individuals who have completed an undergraduate degree in a non-journalism field or are seeking a professional qualification for a career in journalism.

Led by industry professionals and academics, students will have the opportunity to publish their work within the program.

Benefiting from strong partnerships with national organizations such as Sky Sports News, The Independent, The Sun, Daily Star, TalkSPORT, and the Mail Online.

- Recognized by the Solicitors Regulation Authority and the Bar Standards Board, this LLM enables graduates in non-law-related studies to convert to a career in law.

- Experienced lecturers at Brighton Law School will support students through this practice-led, skills-based course, integrating guest talks from local practitioners and judges.

ACCA membership also provides access to the institute’s resources and the opportunity to network with senior professionals and executives. By following the ACCA’s syllabus for the Strategic Professional stage, students can graduate with a Masters degree or Postgraduate Diploma alongside studying the relevant modules required to become a Chartered Certified Accountant. To gain the ACCA qualification, students must pass the ACCA’s external exams.
courses.66af:
This MSc Accounting course supports the development of students' professional career in business, accounting and financial management. This course is aligned to the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) professional examinations.

Successful completion of the course will enhance students' understanding of financial management and reporting, performance management, risk and corporate governance. Students will develop an understanding of a range of research methods and analytical techniques through an introduction to research methods. The final project module develops students' critical and investigative skills to help them meet their professional interests and career goals. This may take the form of a dissertation, a work-based case study or a new business development proposal.

Successful completion of the MSc Accounting degree will provide students with the valuable skills needed in a variety of financial management and accountancy roles across all sectors.

Program Description

Biomedical Scientists are essential members of the modern healthcare team and, in collaboration with doctors and other medical professions, aid in diagnosis of disease, evaluate effectiveness of treatment, and research into causes and cures of diseases. This course is ideal for those wanting to develop advanced knowledge and skills in Biomedical Science.

Biomedical Scientists are in demand in the healthcare service (NHS pathology labs, National Blood and Transplant Service), medical research, pharmaceutical industry, and organisations such as the UK Health Security Agency and the Medical Research Council.

Students will receive training in the skills required in the reading and interpretation of the literature and translating that into evidence-based practice. The University of Chester aims to develop students' research and writing skills so that they will be in a position to contribute to the scientific literature in an effective manner.

The course culminates in the Research Dissertation, which will be assessed through the students' production of a research article written in the style of publishable scientific work and a short oral presentation. Options could include data or laboratory-based projects, depending on research interests.

Successful completion of this MSc programme can lead to a range of exciting career and research opportunities, including careers in biomedical or clinical research, medicine, physician associate, PhD study or teaching.
courses.6hi5:
Program Description

This exciting course focuses on contemporary issues in family and child psychology, exploring critical issues as families and society become increasingly diverse. Furthermore, this course offers the opportunity to study the interface between family and child psychology and social policy, making its content relevant to students with diverse career objectives.

This course provides an excellent opportunity to study the psychology of the child and family in context, engaging with, and being taught by, leading experts in the field. With a heavily applied focus, students will learn, explore and examine how theory can be used to explain contemporary issues in the area while undertaking training in research methodology and practical issues. Students will also have the opportunity to join the Family, Infant and Child research group and to take part in Department seminars.

This course also emphasises employability skills, embedding a range of professional and practical skills in all of the modules.
courses.75q2:
The MSc Financial Technology (FinTech) and Business Analytics programme is specifically crafted to advance the career prospects of professionals engaged in fintech, data analysis, and business management roles.

Successful completion of this programme will enrich your comprehension of financial technology, data-driven decision-making, Artificial Intelligence applications and coding skills in today's dynamic business landscape.Our programme emphasises real world learning. All our students from the FinTech & Business Analytics programme can access real-world financial and economic datasets powered by Alpha Vantage API.

Furthermore, you will be introduced to an array of research methodologies and analytical techniques. The concluding project module will nurture your critical thinking and investigative aptitude, manifesting in the form of a dissertation, a real-world case study, or a novel business development proposal—all tailored to foster your professional interests and align with your career aspirations.

There is an option to choose a Project/Placement year for this course, at an additional cost.
courses.6z4c:
Students will develop their understanding of the law and boost their employability with Master of Laws (LLM) degree. This year-long course will solidify their knowledge in criminal law and the criminal justice system, looking at contemporary issues and practice.

Graduates will hone their research, academic writing and critical thinking skills with modules including Theory of Criminal Justice, Criminal Law and Domestic and Global Terrorism. They will complete a dissertation on an area of their choice, supported by the University of Chichester expert academics.

Extra-curricular opportunities include pro bono work, mediation, work experience in a law firm or mini pupillage, in addition to mooting competitions, client-interviewing competitions and contributing to the University of Chichester Student Law Review.

This postgraduate degree will prepare students for a career within the criminal justice system or within law more widely.
courses.1x5w:
The Master of Arts in Social Work prepares students for a wide range of experiences and learning opportunities that they will encounter in practice.

Students will gain a combination of effective and relevant skills alongside up-to-date knowledge of how to work effectively with children, adults and a wide range of social problems.

This course begins with a carefully structured induction program, before graduates move on to study modules designed to develop their personal and professional skills. They will be supported throughout by a structured tutorial program; linking university-based learning to practice placements.
courses.1x55:
The Master of Science in International Business prepares graduates to work as a business manager in an international environment. They will explore topics including strategic management, international business, global marketing, finance and accounting, behavioral economics and research methods. If candidates are looking to brush up on their business skills or to expand their current business abroad then this course is for them.

This course develops students' managerial and general business knowledge and skills. When they graduate they will have a strong grounding in international business and be well placed to pursue an international business career in a range of organizations. Students will develop the cultural awareness they need to make an impact in an international commercial environment.
courses.5af3:
The Master of Science in International Business and Finance degree will give students a broad practical knowledge of business administration and finance in the global business context.

Graduates will explore the essential knowledge and skills they need as an international business manager, and study strategy and research modules alongside specialist finance topics. They will complete an independent research project in their final term.

The project will develop students' research, analysis, synthesis and business writing skills. They will focus on a specific business area of their choice that related to International Business and Finance.
courses.8ins:
This dynamic full-time programme offers the opportunity for individuals to extend their professional knowledge, enhancing their career profiles and prospects across a range of roles relevant to their contexts and interests. It provides a deeper understanding and expertise in the field of education, emphasizing the global outlook, cultural fluency, and the significance of social change valued in today’s employment market.

Suitable for educators in various settings, the programme focuses on employability and career advancement skills. It explores how the skills and knowledge gained can optimise employment opportunities. Through employer-led events, career guidance, and introductions to organizations offering optional voluntary practical experience, participants develop their professional profiles and become well-equipped to identify, accelerate, and navigate career progression opportunities.
courses.28ub:
This course is for students who are inspired to work in the global business world with multi-national companies. This course will help them to secure the professional knowledge and skills to bolster their career in this fast-paced market.

Graduates will learn about international business practices, operations, sustainability and strategic management in the context of today’s complex and changing globalised marketplace.

Students will learn in a ‘global classroom’ alongside international students, where they can experience a social and cultural understanding of practice in other countries, helping to inform their cross-cultural business reasoning, practices and solutions. Plus, it gives them the opportunity to secure contacts across the globe.

Graduates’ learning will be enhanced with work-based projects and workshops giving them every opportunity to build their business confidence and give them an authentic insight into the scenarios and challenges that they will face in their future career.
courses.8ptk:
The MSc International Business at the University of Derby focuses on applied analysis in economics, strategy, law, finance, marketing, and human resources, all examined from a global perspective. The programme provides opportunities to engage with regional experts and international business leaders through guest lectures, consultancy projects, case studies, and professional mentoring. Students can enhance their employability and build their CVs through the Futures Award in Leadership in International Business, and gain practical experience using real-world data via Bloomberg to support research into companies and markets worldwide. The programme also offers specialist variants including MSc International Business and Finance, MSc International Business and Marketing, and MSc International Business and HRM.

Designed to meet the needs of today’s business environment, the MSc International Business equips students with a thorough understanding of the economic, financial, legal, and cultural factors affecting international business. The course integrates disciplines such as international business strategy, management and marketing, international economics, and international trade legislation. Drawing on real-world case studies, students develop skills in quantitative analysis and applied research while examining all aspects of business operations in an international context.

The programme maintains high-profile partnerships with leading industry names, including Lloyds Bank Corporate, the Bank of England Midlands Office, HSBC Nottingham, Eversheds, Price Waterhouse Cooper, PKF Cooper Parry, Smiths of Derby, GI Insight, and Kitchencraft, with many contributing through guest lectures. Company visits provide additional insights, with tours of the iPro Stadium, Derby Arena, Crown Derby, and high-performance engineering company epm:technology. Students can extend professional networks through events such as Institute of Directors workshops, company taster days, and the University’s Network of Entrepreneurs.

Professional mentoring is provided to guide career development. Mentors include international trade advisors, banking specialists, and senior managers from partner companies, offering insights into career paths and business practice. Career development planning is embedded within the course, with each student supported by a personal tutor and access to the University’s professional career services, even after graduation.

The programme also prioritises the development of transferable skills and real-world business experience. Students gain expertise using the Bloomberg database, a leading global business resource providing financial and company information, economic data, and market analysis, and can pursue the Bloomberg Market Concepts Certificate. Opportunities are provided to participate in competitions such as the IBM University Business Challenge and the University Trading Challenge, as well as to contribute to regional specialist projects like the economic impact study of the Buxton Festival and the Derby Low Carbon Initiative. Research can also be published in the College of Business Economic Bulletin or in the academic journal Critical Perspectives on Business Management.

The MSc culminates in an Independent Study, allowing students to select a theme aligned with their interests and career ambitions, developing in-depth research and critical thinking skills. Recent research topics have included knowledge transfer in the South African hotel sector, consumer complaint behaviour in Chinese online shopping, leadership challenges in SMEs in the UK and USA, foreign market analysis for Spanish exporters, and social media strategies in the beauty industry.

In addition, students may undertake the Futures Award in Leadership in International Business, which recognises leadership abilities and consultancy skills through extra-curricular activities, including business consultancy projects, volunteering, fundraising, and networking opportunities. Past participants have had the chance to hear from influential regional leaders such as Mel Morris, Chairman of Derby County FC and an early investor in King Digital Entertainment, the company behind the global game phenomenon Candy Crush.
courses.8n91:
This MSc in Artificial Intelligence is for anyone building a career in Artificial Intelligence (specialising in machine learning and deep learning). Students will learn to create intelligent software and algorithms that support better business decisions and help shape strategy in any organisation.

This artificial intelligence (AI) programme gives students advanced knowledge and skills to help design and build machine learning tools for automation, prediction, and smart decision-making.

As an Artificial Intelligence postgraduate, students will learn through a mix of lectures, hands-on workshops using tools like Python, Hadoop, Spark, and Matlab, and lab-based sessions. They will also take part in practical projects, seminars, and work-based learning to build both technical and professional skills.
courses.8na7:
UEL's MSc in International Business Management prepares students for a huge variety of business roles in a global context, whether they are interested in entrepreneurship, global innovation, corporate strategy, consultancy, or multinational management. UEL's staff and students are drawn from all over the world with widely varied expertise, making this MSc a truly international programme.

The course looks toward future trends in business, from the changing role of business in society to the impact that rapidly evolving technology has on business in a global context. The university trains students to be mobile across different markets in high-tech, knowledge-intensive industries; remain flexible in the face of technological change, and maintain an international outlook as the world evolves.

Students will learn about the way businesses can adapt to new challenges, from the importance of sustainability in the face of climate change to the rise of robotics and the Internet of Things.

Based across Docklands and USS campuses, students will have easy access to London City Airport, City Of London Square Mile, Canary Wharf financial and digital district, International Excel Centre and the O2 Arena.

The course is designed to resonate with people from a variety of backgrounds, so students won't need to have specific academic or work experience. Throughout the degree, students will develop crucial analytical, research, and communication skills as they work on projects with their fellow students and undertake their own original research. UEL's personal tutoring scheme also gives students access to bespoke academic advice and exciting industry opportunities.

This course is accredited by the Association for Project Management (APM).

The University of Essex MA Curating offers a practical and theoretical training in devising and curating exhibitions, as students work towards the preparation of an exhibition at Essex's on-site Art Exchange gallery.

This course combines practice, theory and histories of curating in equal measure. Students will develop essential base skills for a successful exhibition – from object handling to managing exhibition budgets – through visiting lectures by active museum professionals; practical workshops using our on-site collection and galleries; and competitive placements at leading institutions. Previous students have worked at the V&A, Royal Academy of Arts, Hayward Gallery and Firstsite Gallery.

Students will build their own confident grasp of the history and theory of exhibition-making, studying with academics who besides being active curators are producing new key texts on the curatorial history and theory. Students study topics including: how an exhibition can be used as a means of social or political critique, the historical role that museums have played in society, participation and social engagement between spectators, artists, and curators, and a choice of history of art options.

Essex is ranked 6th among Art History departments in the UK for research excellence.

The visual arts and culture industries have become an increasingly significant part of the national and international economy, and Essex's art history graduates leave Essex with the skills to take advantage of this growing opportunity.

Graduates from Essex's programmes are ideally prepared for roles in the media, in advertising, in museums and galleries, in education (in schools, universities, and cultural institutions), as conservators, as auctioneers, dealers and antiques specialists, in charities, in publishing, as specialist arts lawyers, as PR agents, in fashion, or to run their own galleries.

Recent graduates have gone on to work for a wide range of high-profile companies including: National Portrait Gallery, Victoria and Albert Museum, Sotheby's New York, Momart Ltd, and John Lewis.

Through studying MA Economics and Public Policy, students will be equipped with an indispensable skillset in critical thinking, communication and argument development and analytics, which are highly sought after by employers today.

They will work with experts from within our Department of Economics, top 5 in the UK for research with over 90% rated as ‘world-leading’ or ‘internationally excellent’ (REF 2014). In addition to the Department of Government, one of the most prestigious in Europe, with an outstanding record of teaching, research and publication.
courses.7a81: This course is for students seeking to take their journalism experience to an advanced level and for students who have no background in journalism but are eager to supplement their academic knowledge with journalism skills. It introduces students to the theory and practice of journalism in a global context. It has an international scope and deals with the practice of journalism across different media, cultural and regulatory environments. Students will have the option to tailor their studies by choosing a practice- or theory-led route depending on their interests and career ambitions. The practice track is useful for students who are coming from other disciplines but want to supplement their knowledge with journalism skills; the theory track is useful for those considering a PhD in journalism studies. The Professional Master’s by Research in Education adopts an active learning approach with a strong emphasis on real-world application, offering a practical and professionally oriented course tailored for international students. The programme encourages interactive learning through discussions, case studies, guest lectures, and collaborative projects, fostering meaningful engagement between students and lecturers, as well as among peers. Designed to be inclusive, the course promotes integration and collaboration among students from diverse cultural and academic backgrounds.

A distinctive feature of the programme is its strong focus on empirical research. Students are given the opportunity to undertake a research project that critically applies educational theories to real-world challenges. This experience enhances their knowledge and understanding while strengthening critical and analytical thinking skills essential for a global career in education.

While lectures and seminars form part of the teaching approach, students are encouraged to engage in small communities of practice—collaborative peer groups based on shared research interests or methodologies. Peer review and constructive feedback are integrated into the learning process to support the development of reflective listening, critical evaluation, and a commitment to action.

The programme promotes the use of technology in learning to maximise engagement, build transferable skills, and enrich the overall educational experience. A ‘bring your own device’ policy encourages students to develop digital literacies, contributing to innovative learning design and dynamic learning activities.

The course experience is further enhanced through live briefs, real-world case studies, staff-led research initiatives, guest speakers, and strong links to industry. These elements provide students with direct pathways to future career opportunities and ensure a rich and applied learning journey.

This professional MA by Research is designed with an active learning approach that emphasises real-world application, creating a practical and industry-focused experience for both international and home students. Teaching is delivered through expert-led lectures, alongside collaborative activities such as group discussions, debates, role play, and professional briefs. The course fosters an inclusive environment that encourages integration and collaboration among students from diverse backgrounds.

Students develop the knowledge, skills, and professional networks needed to pursue a career in Public Relations and communications. The curriculum covers key areas including influencer targeting, social media strategy, campaign planning, crisis communications, media relations, and strategic communications. Practical skills are also developed in video and podcast production, copywriting, and editing using Adobe software, alongside learning the latest digital PR techniques and the evolving role of AI in content creation and the wider PR industry.

The teaching team includes practising PR professionals, supported by guest speakers from leading organisations, offering valuable industry insight and networking opportunities. The study approach combines lectures and seminars with small peer learning communities, where students engage in shared research interests and approaches. Peer review and feedback play a key role in developing critical thinking, reflective listening, and evaluative skills.

A strong emphasis is placed on empirical research, culminating in an independent research project that applies theory to real-world challenges. This enables students to deepen their analytical abilities and operate effectively within a global context. Technology is integrated throughout the course to enhance engagement and build transferable skills.

The programme is enriched through live briefs, real-world case studies, staff research, and industry connections. Students build a professional portfolio that includes communication strategies and multimedia content, supporting their transition into employment. Guest speakers have included organisations such as Sport England, UCAS, BHM, Reach Plc, and various PR agencies.

Prospective students should be aware that this research degree requires a high level of academic commitment throughout its duration. Those planning to bring dependents are advised to carefully consider their arrangements to ensure their studies are not adversely affected.

Program Description

Study and produce creative texts in every genre, explore the latest innovative writing, and learn about cultural contexts, research methods and creative industries within the heart of London.

In this creative writing master's, students will be guided by expert writers through each of the core genres of prose fiction, poetry, scriptwriting and creative non-fiction. They will be able to experiment with topics, styles, forms and hybrids, leading to a substantial portfolio of original creative work.

Among the department's innovative approaches to imaginative writing, they encourage students to explore links between texts and other disciplines, such as history, theory, politics, and cultural studies. Different writing techniques and reflective practices will help students advance their skills in textual analysis and encourage them to consider the opportunities and challenges of writing.

Creative writing graduates will be well-placed to pursue careers in writing, academia, research, journalism, publishing, teaching, and creative and heritage industries, amongst other occupations. courses.1xgi:
The Agriculture for Sustainable Development, MSc course is for graduates and professionals looking for greater knowledge and expertise in sustainable agricultural development. Students will gain a strong understanding of the fundamentals of crop production, such as adaptation to climate and other environmental changes. They then explore how this expertise can help to design effective food production systems without placing unsustainable demands on the environment.

The emphasis is on agriculture in tropical or developing countries, but the approaches can be used globally. The course integrates natural, social and economic sciences. It draws on the department's unrivalled expertise in an array of disciplines, including crop production, pest and disease management, postharvest technologies, climate change adaptation, and agricultural economics and marketing.

The course is taught on Greenwich's Medway Campus and delivered by world-leading scientists from the award-winning Natural Resources Institute (NRI), who are working on sustainable agriculture projects around the world. The department uses real global case studies in its teaching, and students will have an opportunity to play a meaningful role in current research projects. Benefit from small class sizes, quality supervision, and access to cutting-edge research facilities and resources.

Teaching incorporates lectures, seminars, and practical lab-based investigations. The University uses case studies to help students build teamwork and creative problem-solving skills that are valuable in industry. Learners will also take an independent research project, giving them an opportunity to carry out original research in a well-equipped department, supported by staff with diverse interests and experience.

The Agriculture for Sustainable Development course is designed to give students the space for exploratory and independent study. They'll work towards individual and group assignments and undertake the preparation or follow-up work associated with lectures, seminars, integrative assignments and laboratory classes. A research skills module will shape their approach to independent learning, especially for their research project. Greenwich encourages students to take advantage of a range of related extra-curricular opportunities. The faculty hosts regular seminars from NRI staff and external visitors on a range of diverse topics.

Graduates of this course will be equipped for careers in the agricultural research and rural development sector. Potential future workplaces include NGOs, ministries, funding agencies and national and international research institutes. Graduates may also continue onto a research degree (MPhil or PhD), which will train them for research leadership roles in agriculture and rural development.

By exploring these biological systems, students will learn to develop the technology, tools and products used in research, industry and agriculture.

This course course also includes a research project. If students wish, they can earn an endorsement in Pharmaceutical Biotechnology by taking their project in a pharmaceutical science or a related area.

Potential career destinations include pharmaceutical, agricultural, environmental and biotechnology industries and consultancies, as well as Biomedical and Intellectual property rights agencies. It is also a fine pathway to a research degree.

Many of the projects undertaken by students reflect the key research interests of the department, such as manufacturing, bulk materials handling and instrumentation. However, projects are also derived from the university's links with industry or from students' own interests or experiences.

Lectures are delivered by members of the School of Engineering who have the relevant globally recognised specialism within the respective field. Guest speakers bring additional perspectives from industry or research and keep students updated with the latest industry standards in their discipline.

The taught modules are informed by research and the theory of each topic is accompanied by practical elements covering paper-based, computer-based and hands-on building type challenges.

They'll work towards individual and group assignments and undertake the preparation or follow-up work associated with lectures, seminars, integrative assignments and laboratory classes. MArch Architecture & Urbanism is a Masters of Architecture award within the Design programme at the School of Creative Arts. Within the programme there is strong emphasis on professional practice and the real-world applications of design. Students will develop key research skills and gain a good understanding of the work of other practitioners in their field.

The aim of the postgraduate programme is to equip students with the skills, knowledge and understanding required to practice at an advanced level, to foster their creativity and enhance their employment opportunities. Students will work alongside artists and designers who are involved with a wide variety of media and forms and will benefit from visiting architects and design professionals. Induction, seminars and social events for students and staff mean that they will be part of a friendly and supportive postgraduate community, which also includes film makers, musicians and professionals working in new media. Senior research staff and internationally renowned artists work with postgraduate students, helping students to develop original and challenging work.

This MA Public Relations and Digital Communications course will enable students develop an understanding of the challenges in the PR and communications industry and apply the knowledge from the course to identify effective solutions to real-life case studies.Feel confident and prepared to work in the industry. This course incorporates theoretical and practical learning styles to equip student for a career in the field. This includes traditional lectures as well as workshops, masterclasses and online study.
