university-of-derby.about:
The University of Derby is pushing the boundaries of knowledge to create a better, fairer, and more sustainable future for everyone. Their thriving community of researchers, professionals, and practitioners influence the creation of new knowledge by sharing their expertise. The university's students learn in state-of-the-art facilities, and the university plays a key role in the communities of Derby and Derbyshire.

Research lives in the University of Derby's classrooms. They explore, innovate, and discover solutions to the challenges facing all now and in the future – in the city, region, and across the world. The University applies this in their teaching, powering the next generation of gamechangers, nurturing talent, and helping their students to develop the skills, resilience, and curiosity they will need to make an impact.

Why University of Derby - Derby

  • Location: The Derby Campus is made up of several different sites. Getting between them and the halls of residence couldn't be easier. Whether students are heading to lectures or into town, they can hop on to the University's Unibuses or enjoy a walk to unwind. Derby sits in the centre of England, and it is close to the M1 and M6 motorways, as well as being within easy reach of East Midlands Airport. By train, students can get to London in 90 minutes or to Birmingham in 35 minutes.
  • Facilities: Kedleston Road in Derby is home to the University's fantastic Sports Centre, four-storey library, and spacious study areas. Students will also find plenty of places to eat and socialise with their friends, including Starbucks, Subway, the Union of Students' café and bar, and much more.
  • Research and Innovation: The University of Derby's Innovation and Research Strategy (IRS) drives its ambition to be internationally recognised for high-quality research. Through six Academic Research Themes, they unite expertise across colleges to enhance research excellence and tackle global challenges.
  • Recognition: The University of Derby has been recognised as 2nd for employability and course quality by Uni Compare in 2026. It was also recognised as 1st in the East Midlands for International by Whatuni Student Choice Awards 2025, and no.1 for Accommodation by the Global Student Living Awards 2024, 2023, 2022.
  • Investment in the Future of Business Education: Opened in September 2025, the £75 million Cavendish Building is a seven-storey development in Derby city centre. It has been purpose-built to drive collaboration between students, academics, and industry, with a focus on solving real-world challenges. It boasts state-of-the-art, flexible learning spaces that promote collaboration, creativity, and connectivity, including a high-tech Creativity Lab to unlock new ideas, a fully equipped Trading Floor with Bloomberg and London Stock Exchange Group terminals, a specialist Supply Chain Lab, and an immersive Extended Reality Suite to develop learning in a virtual environment.

university-of-east-london.about:
The University of East London was founded in 1898 with the aim of serving both its local community and a wider audience. The University believes that education is a potent tool in decreasing inequality and promoting a brighter future for everyone. UEL is reshaping education for the benefit of all, giving students from any background the skills and opportunities to thrive in the modern world.

The University of East London equips students for a rewarding career with work placements, networking opportunities, and tools to navigate the unexpected. Their graduates - whether artists, architects, or accountants - are making a real impact in their communities.

Why University of East London (UEL)

  • Location: UEL is one of the only London-based universities to have a self-contained campus. They are part of the local community and well-connected to the rest of London, and the world - City Airport is at their doorstep. Full of culture, creativity and career opportunities, East London is one of the youngest, most multicultural neighbourhoods in the UK, so students will fit in no matter where they’re from.
  • Careers-Led University: UEL is a careers-first university, offering education and industry access to people from all walks of life. With ambition and hard work, students can turn their goals into reality through UEL's contacts, expertise, and support. Their academics, often active in their industries, guide students through courses designed to address real-world challenges. The University collaborates with industry to constantly update its courses, ensuring that education aligns with evolving employer needs, preparing students for a rewarding career.
  • Stand Out From the Crowd: Why do University of East London graduates stand out? It's because they offer employers more than just academic expertise. UEL has designed their degree programmes to include essential skills to help students adapt, embrace change and show potential employers that they are fit for the careers of the future. UEL's Professional Fitness and Mental Wealth programme develops students' emotional, cultural and cognitive intelligence alongside digital skills, communication, resilience and entrepreneurship.
  • Diverse and Supportive Community: At the University of East London, students will benefit from learning alongside people from all over the world. UEL is diverse, inclusive, and supportive. Students will feel welcomed and supported throughout their university journey and beyond - from application and beyond into career.

university-of-essex.about:
The University of Essex is a school where curiosity prevails, and where exploring new ways of thinking and pushing boundaries, isn’t just encouraged, it’s expected. The University of Essex was named University of the Year at the Times Higher Education Awards 2018 for their determination to do things differently and put student success at the centre of everything they do.

Essex boasts a massive 350-mile coastline, the 2nd longest of any county in England. There’s plenty to explore across the county, from countryside walks to award-winning beaches. Students can even try a plate of freshly caught oysters, or take a boat trip from Walton-on-the Naze to see the local seals! There’s lots for students to explore, and it is just a short train ride from London. This makes it great for students because they can enjoy being near the capital, but with a lower cost of living.

Join a bold and brilliant community of learning at the University of Essex, home to radical thinking and challenging ideas since the 1960s!

Why University of Essex - Colchester Campus

  • Gold-Rated Teaching: The University of Essex has a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF). This means that the teaching quality, learning environments and student outcomes students can look forward to are among the best in the UK.
  • Campus: The University of Essex’s Colchester-based campus is well equipped to support each students’ studies. They will have access to a 6-floor library, IT suites and even a cinema! Other great on-campus amenities include a sports centre, hair salon, shops and restaurants. The campus is set around a tranquil lake and has lots of resident wildlife, so students can study in a beautiful natural environment.
  • Historic County: The University of Essex in Colchester is located in the county of Essex, which is home to an incredible coastline and many historic villages. The county of Essex has an important place in British culture and history. Colchester is the oldest recorded town in the UK, and the first capital of Roman Britain. Today, Colchester is a popular town, with a great mix of historic buildings and modern attractions. Students can go shopping, eat at a wide range of restaurants, head to the local bars and pubs, and even explore the town’s zoo.
  • Diversity and Support: Join a community of 140+ nationalities with diverse cultures and ideas. The University of Essex understands the needs of international students, and offers special mentoring sessions, academic and language support, and one-on-one guidance.
  • Innovative Spirit: Students are encouraged to think independently and question convention. They will learn how to think creatively, and how to apply their knowledge and ideas to real-life situations. They’ll also benefit from the University of Essex's partnerships with over 300 institutions all over the world, and the chance to do a paid internship either during their degree or within 3 years of graduating

university-of-essex-international-colleg.about:
The University of Essex was founded in the 1960s as an innovative institution to challenge traditional thinking. It is highly ranked in many subjects, giving students the chance to advance their education in a field they love. It offers a beautiful main campus just outside the city of Colchester, which is only 1 hour from London by train. Essex is a hugely international university, with students of 140+ nationalities bringing great diversity of cultures and ideas, creating a truly global campus community.

Opened in 2018, the University of Essex International College is run by Kaplan International Pathways, and offers degree preparation courses in partnership with the University of Essex. These on-campus courses allow students to meet the University’s entry requirements, and progress to a bachelor’s or master’s degree. The College offers customised teaching and support for international students, who’ll also enjoy access to University of Essex facilities from day one. These include academic, sports and social facilities, plus clubs and societies, giving students the full Essex experience.

Why University of Essex International College (Kaplan International Pathways)

  • Expert Support: College staff are dedicated to helping international students and offer wide-ranging support. This includes adapting to life in Essex and the UK, academic and personal development, making new friends, resolving queries and challenges, and many other aspects of living and studying abroad.
  • Ideal Accommodation: On their pathway course, students can live in University of Essex accommodation that’s perfectly placed on campus, with easy access to classes, facilities and Colchester city centre.
  • City, country and coast: Essex offers the best of both worlds: beautiful countryside, seaside and towns, within easy reach of metropolitan London. Nearby Colchester has everything you need for a fun and fulfilling student experience. Students can go shopping, eat at a wide range of restaurants, head to the local bars and pubs, explore Roman history and even explore the city’s zoo. The wider county of Essex offers beautiful countryside and stunning coastline to explore – ideal for day trips and weekend excursions.
  • Guaranteed progression: When students pass their course at the International College with the necessary grades and attendance, they’re guaranteed entry to their University of Essex degree.

university-of-glasgow.about:
The University of Glasgow (abbreviated as Glas. in post-nominals; Scottish Gaelic: Oilthigh Ghlaschu) is a public research university in Glasgow, Scotland. Founded by papal bull in 1451 [O.S. 1450], it is the fourth-oldest university in the English-speaking world and one of Scotland's four ancient universities. Along with the universities of St Andrews, Aberdeen, and Edinburgh, the university was part of the Scottish Enlightenment during the 18th century. Glasgow is the second largest university in Scotland by total enrolment and 8th-largest in the United Kingdom.

In common with universities of the pre-modern era, Glasgow originally educated students primarily from wealthy backgrounds; however, it became a pioneer in British higher education in the 19th century by also providing for the needs of students from the growing urban and commercial middle class. Glasgow University served all of these students by preparing them for professions: law, medicine, civil service, teaching, and the church. It also trained smaller but growing numbers for careers in science and engineering.

Glasgow has the fifth-largest endowment of any university in the UK and the annual income of the institution for 2024–25 was £1.05 billion of which £241.1 million was from research grants and contracts, with an expenditure of £982.8 million. It is a member of Universitas 21, the Russell Group and the Guild of European Research-Intensive Universities.

The university was originally located in the city's High Street; since 1870, its main campus has been at Gilmorehill in the City's West End. Additionally, a number of university buildings are located elsewhere, such as the Veterinary School in Bearsden, and the Crichton Campus in Dumfries.

The alumni of the University of Glasgow include some of the major figures of modern history, including James Wilson, a signatory of the United States Declaration of Independence, 3 Prime Ministers of the United Kingdom (William Lamb, Henry Campbell-Bannerman and Bonar Law), 3 Scottish First Ministers (Humza Yousaf, Nicola Sturgeon and Donald Dewar), economist Adam Smith, philosopher Francis Hutcheson, engineer James Watt, physicist Lord Kelvin, surgeon Joseph Lister along with 4 Nobel Prize laureates (in total 8 Nobel Prize winners are affiliated with the university) and numerous Olympic gold medallists, including the current chancellor, Dame Katherine Grainger.

university-of-gloucestershire.about:
The University of Gloucestershire offers a wide range of degrees, courses and apprenticeships at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. Typically, students learn theory from industry experts and put their learning into practice in course work, real-world projects, placements and field trips. The school has a 150-year tradition of education dating back to 1847​. There are over 100 academic courses to choose from and approximately 10,000 students studying at the three campuses in Gloucestershire.

​​​​​Located in the heart of Gloucester, Oxstalls is just 15 minutes’ walk from the city centre giving students easy access to the city’s clubs, bars, shops, theatres, venues and cafes. Oxstalls is also just around the corner from Kingsholm rugby stadium, home to Gloucester Rugby and host to a number of Rugby World Cup matches in 2015. ​In 2018, the University of Gloucestershire's School of Business and Technology moved to the brand-new, state-of-the-art home at the Oxstalls campus. The £18 million development is home to the school's Business, Marketing, Human Resource Management, Law and Accounting and Finance courses.

Why University of Gloucestershire

  • Campus: Located in the heart of Gloucester, the students of Oxstalls benefit from connections to an extensive network of clubs, sports teams, theatres, festivals and venues.
  • Student Life: Explore everything the university has to offer at Freshers' Fayre. This includes BBQs, fancy dress parties and the Freshers' Ball. The Freshers' Fayre is where students can sign up to clubs and societies - and get lots of freebies.
  • Clubs: Get involved in anything of interest including snow club, ukulele, the Bee Project, film, comedy, creative writing, paintballing, Afro-Caribbean and Dumbledore's Army. Students can even start up their own.
  • Athletics: Students who love sport will love Oxstalls' labs and facilities, including the onsite performance lab, strength and conditioning suite, sports therapy clinics, fitness suite, and the all-weather pitch.

NOTE: This school may use UCAS as an external portal for application for some programs. A £20 (single application) or £25 (up to 5 applications) application fee may apply.

university-of-greenwich.about:
Greenwich is more than a collection of individual students and staff, it is a community of people united by their passion for learning. University of Greenwich courses will give you the skills employers value and the confidence to achieve extraordinary things. Our historic campuses in London and Kent offer first-class facilities, inspiring teaching and a friendly, diverse community. Greenwich employs well-qualified, expert teaching staff, the majority with formal teaching qualifications. A large number of our academics have also previously worked in business or industry. You'll benefit from excellent study facilities, including first-class advanced laboratories for science and engineering subjects and three campus libraries with dedicated academic services librarians.

Why the University of Greenwich

Beautiful, inspiring locations: The iconic Greenwich Maritime World Heritage Site receives millions of tourists each year who visit the Royal Observatory meridian line, Cutty Sark ship, historic market, museums and, of course, the ORNC. The campus can be seen in many movies including Skyfall and Pirates of the Caribbean, and TV series such as The Crown.

Facilities to shape your future: Since 2013, the university has invested more than £150 million in laboratories, teaching spaces and student facilities.

Advancing knowledge at Greenwich: Research addresses some of the world's most challenging issues, from global health to public safety. Current investigations include mosquito-carried diseases, such as malaria and the Zika virus, and the use of 3D printers for medical implants. Other projects include life-saving research into evacuating difficult environments, such as high-rise construction sites, and understanding the links between politics and the economy.

Taught by passionate people: Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF) Silver rating in 2017 and Higher Education Academy National Teaching Fellowships for a large number of our teaching staff.

university-of-greenwich-international-co.about:
University of Greenwich International College (UGIC) is an embedded college delivered on the main campus at University of Greenwich, in London. UGIC provides the first stages of the International Incorporated Bachelors and the International Incorporated Masters programs. During the pathway program, students are prepared for university-level studies by learning core subject knowledge while developing their academic English level and study skills. With experienced teachers and small class sizes, students will receive first-class teaching as well as the individual guidance needed to adjust to their new life as a UK university student. UGIC students enjoy full University of Greenwich student status, with access to all University facilities and services.

Following successful completion of a pathway program at UGIC, students can continue their studies directly at University of Greenwich. Established in 1890, University of Greenwich is situated on the banks of the River Thames in London. University of Greenwich is a modern institution with strong industry connections that emphasizes preparing students for careers in a rapidly-changing world. University of Greenwich is part of the University Alliance group and is silver rated in the Teaching Excellence Framework and its renowned research has been globally received and endorsed by nine Times Higher Education Awards and four Queen’s Anniversary Prizes for Higher & Further Education.

Why University of Greenwich International College?

  • Campus: The University of Greenwich's international community includes students from over 140 countries and UGIC is a supportive and welcoming home for international students to learn and make new friends.
  • Facilities: UGIC is based on one of the university's three campuses, where students have full access to facilities, including labs, studios, social and teaching spaces, sports and recreational facilities, and a high-tech library.
  • Location: London is the #1 city for students in the world, home to some of the world's top educational institutions, headquarters of international businesses and organizations, major tourist attractions, as well as entertainment, restaurants and bars, and shopping options that appeal to all tastes. UGIC is only 25 minutes from central London by train.
  • Small Class Sizes: Students are prepared for university studies in the best teaching environment: small classes led by experienced tutors who give each student the support they need!
  • Seamless Transition: Upon successful completion of their studies at UGIC, students can expect a direct and seamless transition onto their course at University of Greenwich.

With a student community of over 25,300 including more than 2,800 international students from 100 different countries, the University has a global network of over 210,000 alumni. It continues to rise up the national rankings.

  • High-Quality Education: The University is of the highest quality in the UK as it has been awarded Gold in the Teaching Excellence and Student Outcomes Framework. Over 96.5% of Herts students are employed within the first six months of graduating.
  • Physical Well-Being: Active Students is an excellent program designed to help students of all backgrounds stay fit and healthy on campus. There is a wide variety of classes to choose from, including Pilates, Weight Training, Smash HIIT, and so much more.
  • Convenient Campus and Facilities: Herts students are surrounded by culture and entertainment to suit all tastes and interests! Some of these include: Access to great music and theatre communities, restaurants on and off-campus, museums and galleries, live sporting events, and outside spaces and parks on and off-campus.

The University of Huddersfield - London campus is specifically dedicated to preparing international students with the skills and knowledge needed to successfully complete a postgraduate degree in business. Choose a Master’s degree that offers the reputation of the University of Huddersfield's teaching quality and employability success as well as all the opportunities that London has to offer! This campus offers not only a top-rate business education, but also support students as they adapt to life in London and take the next step in their careers. The University of Huddersfield is among the UK's top providers of work placement courses and knows exactly how to prepare students for successful careers and a great future.

Why University of Huddersfield - London

  • Facilities: Students get to learn in lecture theatres, small classrooms, and have one-to-one sessions with tutors. They also have access to a library during their studies.
  • Location: Ranked the world’s number one student city (QS Best Student Cities Index 2019), London is also a world-renowned city of thriving commerce where students can develop their interest in business. Close proximity to some of the world’s leading organizations gives students the opportunity to build links and networks that could help progress their careers.
  • Career-Focused Studies: Postgraduate degrees are designed with students' employability in mind. During their studies, students will have the opportunity to gain valuable experience by working for up to 20 hours per week - this will give them a chance to build a network, gain experience in their chosen field and earn some extra spending money.
  • Job Search Support: The university's employability advisers support students to find the right work experience for them by reviewing CVs and cover letters, helping with application forms, interview preparation and more.
  • Education Excellence: This university is gold-rated by the Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF), 2017 and received the Global Teaching Excellence Award from the Higher Education Academy in the same year.
  • Accommodation: International students can live with each other a residence hall in McMillan Student Village, close to their classes. The residence has on-site staff who are there to help students from around the world adjust to life in London.

university-of-kent.about:
Inspire global ambition at the University of Kent, top 40 UK university with outstanding teaching, modern facilities, award-winning student support and vibrant study locations. Over 18,000 students over 100 nations study across its two spacious UK campuses in Canterbury and Medway which are both less than one hour by train to London and close proximity to Europe.

Students who choose Kent for their undergraduate or postgraduate degree will be joining an institution known for its outstanding research, and one that can help students to meet their career goals through excellent support and quality teaching. Beyond that, students are also joining a diverse community of thinkers - critical and creative - who will spark inspiration and challenge students to question their own expertise.

Students will benefit from leading facilities, the latest technology, and a truly supportive environment including various services aimed at supporting any student concerns or obstacles to successful study. The focus of every single degree at Kent is not solely on the subject matter, but also the wider skillsets required to work in that field. As such, wherever possible, real-world experiences are woven into each degree, fully preparing students for their future role.

Students at Kent will benefit from world-class research, outstanding teaching quality and excellent careers guidance too. As well as developing skills in interviewing, finding jobs and building up a wide range of talents, students will earn Employability Points, rewarding the most pro-active students with the best opportunities for internships and more.

Why University of Kent - Canterbury

  • Location: Beautiful, unique, peaceful, and green, the Canterbury campus is built on 300 acres of parkland, with views over the historic city of Canterbury. They aren't called 'The Garden of England' for nothing! There is nature all around with 350 miles of coastline to explore. Nearby, Blean's ancient woodland is home to UK's only wild Bison.
  • Education and Student Experience: Kent's students are diverse, passionate and independent, and the University's award-winning support and inspirational teachers make sure students are at the heart of everything they do.
  • Research and Innovation: The University of Kent's research changes lives. It protects the environment, influences policy, solves problems for businesses and supports the most vulnerable. As part of their brilliant research community, students' work can have ground-breaking impact. Explore Kent's five principal areas of research strength: Creativity, Culture and Heritage, Cyber Security, Digital Technology and Communication, Health, Social Care and Wellbeing, Social Justice, Inequalities and Conflict, and Sustainability, Environment and Natural Resources
  • Engagement, Impact and Civic Mission: Canterbury, Kent's historic base, has been a seat of learning for centuries, while they are at the heart of Medway's bid for City of Culture 2025.
  • Arts, Culture, and Entertainment: Developing one's creative side is easy at Kent. Students could produce written, video or audio content at Kent's student media centre; join a drama, dance or stand-up society; sing in a choir; play in a band or in their symphony orchestra. The University is a dynamic and diverse community full of ideas creating exciting new perspectives from a range of backgrounds.

university-of-kent-international-college.about:
University of Kent International College is an embedded college on the Canterbury campus at University of Kent. It is a specialist embedded pathway college, where international students can begin their studies at University of Kent in partnership with Oxford International Education Group.

We prepare you for the future

Whatever your ambitions are, they’re never too bold for Kent; we’ve helped our students achieve some amazing things. By building real-world experience into your degree, with facilities that mirror those you’ll encounter in industry, we prepare you to hit the ground running so you’ll have a serious advantage when you graduate. Our Careers and Employability Service also help you with your future plans, from CV guidance to connecting you with employers at over 600 careers events every year.

We’re world-leading for research

Our reputation for world-leading research was confirmed by our outstanding results in the Research Excellence Framework 2021. For you, this means you’ll learn from leading thinkers whose work informs their teaching. It also means that you’ll be joining a community that pushes boundaries, that is ambitious, innovative and intent on making a positive difference to people’s lives.

We’re making a positive impact

We’re committed to making the world a better, more sustainable and equitable place. That’s why we’re responding to the United Nations’ urgent call for action by embedding their Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into everything we do. Our FutureProof framework gets staff and students involved in the SDGs and inspires them to take action to ensure that we deliver a university of the future.

At the heart of campus are cafés, restaurants and bars, as well as student accommodation, a four-storey library, nightclub, sports centre, theatre and cinema. Getting around is easy too; you can walk across campus in 15 minutes.

university-of-lancashire.about:
University of Lancashire - Preston Campus is right at the heart of the city. You'll find us minutes away from a vibrant shopping centre, attractions and nightlife. It’s home to a thriving international community of over 42,000 students and staff.

Why University of Lancashire - Preston

  • Mission: University is proud of their mission and they take it seriously. Since being founded as the Institution for the Diffusion of Knowledge in 1828, their educational ethos has brought life-changing learning to local people, this remains at the heart of their mission. University institution motto ‘Ex solo ad solem’ translates to ‘From the Earth to the Sun’. It means helping talented people from all walks of life to make the most of their potential. They create positive change in their students, staff, business partners and wider communities, enabling them to develop their full potential by providing excellent higher education, innovation and research.They are a proud civic anchor too, committed to adding social value and playing their role in the economic prosperity of the places in which they are based; sourcing products and services locally, boosting jobs and economic growth. There pride themselves on universally supporting their people, being actively liberating, inherently innovative and proudly spirited to face whatever life throws at us. These values are woven into the fabric of who they are and will always be.
  • Values and initiatives: University of Lancashire - Preston values reflect who they are as a university and what they stand for. They define the things that are most important to us and nurture University's sense of shared purpose. Supporting their values and initiatives are a number of networks, creating positive change throughout their university, for their students, colleagues and the wider communities.
  • Sustainability: The University is a Gold Tier University in the Green Universities Report 2023 (USwitch), highlighting University's commitment to sustainability. They have retained a 2:1 classification in the People & Planet University Green League 2023/24, where they also ranked first place in the North West for water reduction. The University is also one of just 13 universities worldwide to achieve a Bronze Carbon Literate Organisation status.

university-of-law.about:
The University of Law is one of the UK's leading professional law schools, with an unrivalled reputation for innovation and excellence in legal learning. Their first-class global connections means they are uniquely placed to help aspiring lawyers, legal professionals and legal employers of all types achieve their ambitions.

What really sets the University of Law apart from other universities is their guiding principle that future lawyers and business leaders should learn in a realistic, professional and contemporary context, with plenty of practical interactive engagement. That's why they keep their contact hours high and their teaching groups small.

The University of Law's track record of excellence in learning and development has helped them establish worldwide connections within the legal and business industries. This is why many leading global law firms and businesses work exclusively with the University of Law to develop their people, and why employers of all types want to meet University of Law students. It’s why law schools and professional bodies around the world choose to enter into strategic alliances with the University of Law.

The University of Law has a vast network in the legal industry and deliver legal training to 94 of the top 100 law firms, with exclusive relationships with 60 of the top UK law firms and many of the most prestigious US firms in the UK.

The Birmingham campus is located in the city’s Jewellery Quarter, just a short walk away from the centre of the city and other universities – making it a great place to study. The campus has a café, allowing students to grab hot and cold food whilst on the go and, with great transport links and the Birmingham Snow Hill Train Station just round the corner, students are never far from the rest of the UK.

What sets this campus apart is the availability of real law court room furniture, giving students the chance to practise, get hands on experience and feel a part of the law profession before their careers have even begun.

Why the University of Law

  • Heritage: The University of Law is the largest provider of legal education in the UK, tracing their origins to 1876 with the formation of tutorial firm Gibson & Weldon, and in 2016, they opened their leading Business School.
  • Networking: With an alumni network of over 71,000, graduates can stay connected, remain informed and take advantage of a wealth of specially negotiated privileges and discounts. The Alumni Network connects students to over 11,800 businesses and organisations worldwide, allowing them to tap into an incredible pool of alumni talent.
  • Innovative and Contemporary Teaching Practices: All of the University of Law's courses – from their undergraduate law degrees to their diverse range of business courses and postgraduate programmes – are designed with a unique, varied and innovative learning approach proven to deliver self-reliant professionals who can compete in the fast-changing professional world.
  • Focused on Employability: The school focuses exclusively on practice-based training and gives students access to expert Careers and Employability service database as soon as they accept their offer. Students also benefit from University of Law's pioneering and award-winning pro bono programmes, which allow them to gain valuable work experience by helping real clients from the local community.

university-of-lincoln.about:
Set against the backdrop of a beautiful and historic city, the University of Lincoln sits at the heart of it all on the picturesque Brayford Pool waterfront, with almost everything students will need either on campus or just a short walk away.

Established in 1996, the university has flourished into a diverse, internationally recognised university which welcomes thousands of students each year from around the world. In November 2023, the University of Lincoln was awarded the Queen's Anniversary Prize, the UK's highest award for universities, to recognise its work supporting the agri-food sector.

Throughout this exciting period of development, the university has been guided by a consistent set of principles which remain at the heart of its approach today: excellence in teaching, learning, and quality of student experience; responsiveness to the needs of communities and organisations; and working in partnership to make great things happen.

Why University of Lincoln - Brayford Pool

  • Future Ready Degree Courses: University of Lincoln's degree courses are packed with features to help students develop the skills and expertise that employers are looking for. Many of their courses are accredited by recognised and respected organisations, such as the Chartered Management Institute, and include employability, professional practice, or work-based learning modules that can help students apply theory to practice.
  • Industry Insights: The university's Futures Programme provides opportunities to hear from inspiring guest speakers, who are invited to talk about their careers and to discuss emerging industry trends. Students can also access Lincoln Connect, which is the University of Lincoln’s online mentoring platform, where they can develop their networking skills and build a professional community.
  • Teaching of the Highest Quality: The University of Lincoln was awarded Gold in the national Teaching Excellence Framework 2023 and a five-star score overall in the QS Stars rating 2023
  • Award Winning Student Support: Ranked in the top 10 in the UK for postgraduate support in the Postgraduate Taught Experience Survey 2024
  • A Great Location: Lincoln is regarded as one of England’s great historic cities, and was named the UK’s most affordable student city in the NatWest Student Living Index 2025.

The University of Lincoln offers a great range of accommodation options within the city-centre, the majority of which are located on the Brayford Pool campus or a short walk away. With five residences to choose from, the University offers a variety of options to suit different needs and budgets.

Staying in university managed accommodation includes a range of benefits such as 24/7 security, on-site maintenance, contents insurance, access to classes and workout space at the University’s on-campus Sports Centre and more.

In 2025, the University of Lincoln was listed in the top 5 in the Halls and Student Accommodation category at the Whatuni Student Choice Awards 2025. Lincoln is also ranked 5th out of 100 UK institutions in the Uni Compare Top Universities for Accommodation 2026.

The University of Liverpool International College (UoLIC) offers pathway courses in partnership with the University of Liverpool, and is situated on the University campus. The College is fully equipped to help students follow their path to the prestigious University of Liverpool, with dedicated and experienced staff ready to support them every step of the way. Students can now study in a brand new, state-of-the-art College building with integrated accommodation, which opened in January 2020.

Based on University of Liverpool's campus in Liverpool, the College is fully integrated with the University and UoLIC students are given full access to university facilities while they prepare for their degree. 51 nationalities were represented by new students at the College in 2020. UoLIC offers courses to prepare students for both undergraduate and postgraduate degrees. The Foundation Certificate at University of Liverpool International College is designed to prepare students for entry to an undergraduate degree in a number of subject areas. UoLIC also offer a pathway for a Pre-Master's course to prepare international students for studying at postgraduate level at the University of Liverpool.

Why University of Liverpool International College

  • Rewarding Experience: Staff at the College make sure students get the most out of their experience studying abroad. They'll arrange trips where students can make new friends and see more of the city, and they'll be there to support students at every stage of their path to university.
  • Cultural Hub: Liverpool is a major cultural hub for the north of England. The University has adopted the same international and cultural diversity as the city itself. Liverpool thrives off its multicultural community. Students will be able to enjoy fantastic art galleries and museums like Tate Liverpool and the Beatles Story Museum, as well as many independent shops and cafes. It's a great place to be an international student.
  • Accommodation: When students study at the University of Liverpool International College, they can stay at the new Kaplan Living residence in the same building. university-of-manchester.about:
The University of Manchester is a public research university in Manchester, England, with its main campus south of the city centre on Oxford Road. It is a red brick university, a product of the civic university movement of the late 19th century. The current institution was formed in 2004 through the merger of the University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology (UMIST) and the Victoria University of Manchester. This merger followed a century of close collaboration between the two institutions.

UMIST traced its origins to the Manchester Mechanics' Institution, founded in 1824. The present University of Manchester regards this date, alongside that of the foundation of the ancestor of the Royal School of Medicine and Surgery—one of the predecessor institutions of the Victoria University of Manchester—as its official foundation year. The founders of the Mechanics' Institution believed that all professions depended, to some extent, on scientific principles. The institute therefore taught working individuals those branches of science relevant to their existing occupations, in the belief that practical application would encourage innovation and advancement within those fields. The Victoria University of Manchester was founded in 1851 as Owens College. Academic research undertaken by the university has been published via the Manchester University Press since 1904.

Manchester is the third-largest university in the United Kingdom by total enrolment and receives over 92,000 undergraduate applications per year, making it the most popular university in the UK by volume of applications. The University of Manchester is a member of the Russell Group, the N8 Group, and the US-based Universities Research Association. The university additionally owns and operates major cultural assets such as the Manchester Museum, the Whitworth art gallery, the John Rylands Library, the Tabley House Collection and the Jodrell Bank Observatory, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The university and its predecessor institutions have had 26 Nobel laureates among their past and present students and staff.

university-of-reading.about:
The University of Reading has been at the forefront of UK higher education for nearly a century. Over the decades, they have become innovators and pioneers, pushing academic boundaries and leading social change. They want to inspire innovative and creative approaches to teaching and learning by working in partnership with staff and with the student community. Home to more than 19,000 students, the University of Reading is proud to welcome staff and students from all of the world. Their award-winning campuses house contemporary study facilities, halls of residence, support services, cafés and bars.

University of Reading strives to create a stronger, better University of Reading, building on their past to create an exceptional future. Their four guiding principles form the foundation of Reading's strategy: a genuine love of learning; creating new knowledge; embracing and celebrating diversity of people and ideas; and caring for our environment.

The University of Reading is among the top 30 UK universities in world rankings (ranked 29th out of 84 UK universities featured in the QS World University Rankings 2020) and 98% of their research is rated as being of international standing (Research Excellence Framework, 2014). As a result, the University is already a key partner for businesses of all sizes, from multinational corporations to growing, innovative SMEs.

Why University of Reading

  • Campus: University of Reading's main campus is set in 130 hectares of beautiful parkland, so students will find plenty of places to relax during the day. The campus has won nine consecutive Green Flag awards, recognizing it as one of Britain’s top green spaces.
  • Community: The University has a wide range of events and activities for students to take part in. Whether it's public events, museums, a cinema, public lectures or the SportsPark, there is plenty for students to get involved in.
  • Local Area: The Oracle shopping centre is home to the big names in retail, but there are also independent stores and boutiques around town too. Students will also find plenty of green spaces to relax in and a huge range of cuisines from around the world. Club venues and bars extend beyond campus as Reading town centre transforms from day to night. Discover festivals and new music acts, unique club events and cocktail bars or indulge in one of the late-night ice cream parlours.

university-of-roehampton.about:
The University of Roehampton is a modern university located in south-west London, near the affluent and picturesque Richmond. Students can enjoy living and learning on a beautiful green campus whilst making the most of all the leisure, cultural, sporting, and networking opportunities London has to offer. The university evolved from four teacher training colleges, the first of which, Whitelands College, was established in 1841. The others are Digby Stuart (1874), Froebel College (1892), and Southlands College (1970s), which together make up the now modern campus.

In 1975, the four institutions federated to create Roehampton Institute of Higher Education, which became the University of Roehampton in 2011. The university retains a collegiate format, so students have the opportunity to create bonds with other students in their college as well as on their course.

The University of Roehampton offers a unique academic experience; a beautiful, vibrant parkland campus environment in the heart of bustling south-west London, only 30 minutes from the West End.

The University of Roehampton prides themselves on the guarantee that they make to all of their students: high levels of contact time with excellent teachers and researchers working at the cutting edge of their subject areas.

The mission of the University of Roehampton is simple. The University of Roehampton supports all of their students, whatever their background, to reach their full potential and prepare them for successful graduate careers. the University of Roehampton offers a diverse, dynamic curriculum of programmes delivered by academic staff engaged in world-class research.

Why University of Roehampton

  • World class research: The University of Roehampton's research informs policy, enriches culture, improves people's lives, and is ranked the most research intensive modern university in the UK, meaning that students will be taught by leading experts right from their first year.
  • Career-focused degrees: Students will have exclusive access to an online careers portal, which includes skill builder courses, a jobs database, a CV writing tool, and free careers assessments.
  • Student support: Throughout their students, students will have a tutor who will provide personal study advice. The University of Roehampton also has a wide range of support services for students to use, including financial guidance and health and wellbeing support.
  • Guaranteed accommodation: The University of Roehampton offers guaranteed university accommodation to international students who apply by the application deadline.

It is one of the largest universities in the UK, offering students excellent opportunities and prospects. South Wales is an exceptional part of the UK, with city life, countryside and coast. With campuses located in Cardiff, Newport, Pontypridd and Dubai, 95% of graduates work or study within six months of graduation (DLHE 2016/17). All of these campuses are easily reached by road, rail and air, so wherever students come from, they’re never far from home.

A modern, ambitious university, the University of South Wales makes a real difference to the lives of students, staff and the communities which surround it. With campuses in Cardiff, Newport, Pontypridd and Dubai, the University is renowned for its partnerships with major employers. Their industry connections and emphasis on equipping students with real world experiences make their graduates among the most employable in the UK. And throughout everything they do, they strive to stay true to their core values of being Professional, Responsive, Inspiring and Creative.

Why The University of South Wales

  • Work Placements: Several courses offered at South Wales University guarantee work placements, while the Business and Management, Engineering, Computing and Science and Creative Industries faculties offer the opportunity to work in industry for a year.
  • Study Abroad: ERASMUS+ is the European Union programme for training, youth and sport offering exciting opportunities for participants to study, work, volunteer, teach and train abroad.
  • Employability: The University works hard to ensure that students are ready to start a successful career as soon as they graduate. They have even made employability part of the curriculum, with teaching informed by what happens in the real world and skills students will need for the workplace.
  • High Quality Education: Many courses at the University have been accredited by professional bodies. This means they are of the highest standard and can grant students exemptions from professional exams as an added extra.

university-of-southampton.about:
Reputation, Research and Impact

The University of Southampton is one of the world’s leading universities. With over 150 years of history, they are a founding member of the Russell Group, consistently placed in the top 100 universities in the world by the QS World University Rankings. The University is ranked 87 in the 2026 QS World University Rankings.

92 per cent of their research output was assessed in the latest Research Excellence Framework (REF 2021) as being world leading and internationally excellent, confirming their status as one of the UK’s leading research-intensive universities. This international outlook and reputation attract staff from across the world, with over 25 per cent coming from outside the UK.

Innovative thinking and pioneering research are at the heart of the University of Southampton's culture. Their people are finding solutions for some of the biggest challenges that this planet is facing, pursuing environmental sustainability, and making a difference to the world.

This is the place where fibre-optic research is creating a faster, smarter internet; where the immune system is leading the fight against cancer; where expertise is tackling the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance; and where resources are being secured for the world’s growing populations.

The university stands for exploration and curiosity, interdisciplinary thinking, inventive education and cutting-edge facilities to catalyse change. They inspire minds, bring people and ideas together and give them the space and support to grow, create, ignite, and realise their potential.

Community and Connections

Home to over 25,000 students from more than 130 countries, with around 6,000 members of staff, the University of Southampton is proud of the diverse, vibrant, and welcoming people who make up its university community.

Outside of the UK, they educate students through the University of Southampton Malaysia, a new campus in Delhi, India, collaborations with prestigious partners such as Xiamen University in China, Singapore Institute of Management, Nanyang Technological University and Worldwide Universities Network members, and through Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs).

Once Southampton students become graduates, they join a global community of over 285,000 alumni and can access a network that can provide further opportunities across the world.

Based in a growing city full of opportunities, Southampton is the perfect place to take work further and discover what one is capable of; from turning an idea into reality and making a real difference, to finding new passions and discovering the next step.

The cost of living is roughly £300-£390 per week, which includes accommodation, food, travel, and social life. Southampton is roughly 30% cheaper to live in than London!

Industry and Enterprise

The University of Southampton forges and nurtures connections with industry and organisations, develops new businesses and supports the next generation of leaders and thinkers to achieve their potential.

The university has a strong culture of enterprise. They are ranked third in the UK for consultancy by the latest Higher Education Business and Community Interaction Survey, 2022/23, and more than 150 international businesses have chosen Southampton as a major research partner. In the past few years, strategic partnerships have been developed or expanded with GSK, Rolls-Royce, QinetiQ, IBM, BAE Systems, Airbus, Microsoft, DePuy, Philips, Vitacress, Eli Lilly, and Google ─ to name but a few.

The University of Southampton are also renowned for commercialising its research; its business incubation partnership, SETsquared, is the most influential university business incubator globally. They have an extensive portfolio of partnerships across the world, and through research, they influence governments, businesses, and individuals to make a real impact.

The accommodation office will be available to support and provide advice as to where UWTSD students stay so you can be around students studying with us.

For more details - Kindly refer to the website.

university-of-west-london.about:
The University of West London draws on a heritage of over 150 years in teaching and professional education. From the outset, it has played, and continues to play, a significant role in the educational, cultural, and economic life of its region. Over the years, leading academic institutions, career-focused training providers, and industry specialists have come together to shape what it is today—a university dedicated to students’ careers.

Students are taught by industry professionals with connections to global networks in their chosen fields, and many courses offer the opportunity to undertake placement years where applicable, alongside lifelong careers advice after graduation. The University offers a wide range of high-quality facilities, including an industry-standard Boeing 737 flight simulator, radio, TV and film production studios, nursing simulation centres, music recording suites, and professional kitchens. Beyond the classroom, London becomes an extended campus, offering access to world-class museums, theatres, and landmarks, and the chance to experience one of the most diverse cultural environments in the world.

Why University of West London (UWL)

  • London Location, Local Community: Studying at the University of West London’s West London Campus offers the best of both worlds, with a vibrant local community and beautiful parks nearby, alongside easy access to the energy of central London just a few stops away on the Tube.
  • Great Employment Prospects: Industry-led teaching and specialist careers advice make studying at the University of West London a strong choice for future career success. Students have opportunities to search for placements, engage with employers to gain hands-on experience, and receive tailored, lifelong careers counselling and support.
  • Learning with Industry Experts: Courses at the University of West London are taught by industry experts, and students benefit from their insight, experience, and support as they prepare for their future careers. The University’s consistently high standard of teaching has been recognised with a Silver award in the Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF).
  • Personal Support: Starting university brings a range of new opportunities and challenges, which is why the University of West London provides support every step of the way, offering advice on careers, placements, finances, accommodation, health, faith, and study skills. Even before students begin life at UWL, support is available with guidance on applications, funding, and accommodation.
university-of-west-london.accommodation:
Applicants to the University of West London can benefit from guaranteed accommodation designed to be secure, supportive, and social—helping them feel at home throughout their studies. The University recognises that accommodation is a key part of the student experience and has partnered with local, purpose-built providers to offer competitive rates that are often better than booking directly. By arranging accommodation through the University, applicants also receive additional support throughout the booking process.

Chapter White City, located in East Acton, provides convenient access to Ealing Broadway station as well as the University’s shuttle bus, which serves the Ealing and Brentford campuses. With nearby Central Line stations, central London is just 20 minutes away.

The Paragon, opening in September 2026, offers modern student accommodation just a 10-minute journey from St Mary’s Road. A free and frequent shuttle service connects the Paragon to the Ealing campus, making travel to lectures straightforward and stress-free.

university-of-westminster.about:
University of Westminster - a global university with London energy

Since 1838, the University of Westminster has been helping students from all backgrounds to achieve their potential. And, with over 19,000 students from 160 different countries, University of Westminster is proud to be one of the most diverse universities in the UK.

The university's courses are career-focused and often professionally accredited to give applicants practical skills and professional expertise they need for their future career.

Across four campuses, including three in central London, students will be taught in world-class teaching facilities. The university's location gives students easy access to the city's financial centre, leading international employers and an endless choice of social and cultural attractions from music, restaurants and bars to theatres, libraries and world-class museums.

The Marylebone Campus is within walking distance of Regent's Park and home to the Westminster Business School. It features the Westminster Boardroom, Bloomberg Financial Markets Suite, cutting-edge fabrication lab, exhibition space and an extensive library. From this site, the university offers undergraduate and postgraduate courses including:

  • Accounting and Finance
  • Business and Management
  • Construction, Surveying and Real Estate
  • Data Science and Informatics
  • Economics
  • Marketing
  • Tourism and Events Management
  • Transport and Logistics
  • And Architecture, which belongs to the School of Architecture and Cities

Why University of Westminster - Marylebone

  • Excellent Location: With three campuses in central London and a creative hub in Harrow, north-west London, you'll study in one of the most culturally rich, vibrant cities in the world, which is regularly voted one of best places to be a student according to the QS Best Student Cities Ranking.
  • Career-Building Opportunities: Leading national and multinational companies plus thousands of pioneering start-ups are based in London, making it a great place to meet potential employers, build your network and gain valuable experience to kick-start your career.
  • Practical and professionally accredited courses: University of Westminster's courses are designed with input from industry and leading professional bodies to give students the skills employers need.
  • Comprehensive Careers Support: Award-winning careers service provides advice, access to work placements and mentoring schemes. The university's team will help students find work after they graduate and will continue to support them for three years after graduation.
  • State-of-the-art Facilities: The university's industry-standard facilities include recording studios, cutting-edge fabrication lab, science laboratories, film and television studios, extensive libraries and financial market suites.
university-of-westminster.accommodation:
Students need to plan their accommodations well in advance of their arrival as all accommodation options fill up quickly, well before the start of the semester.

On-Campus Residence Accommodations

On-Campus residence accommodations are provided per discretion by the school.

Off-Campus Accommodations

The local area has a variety of off-campus rental housing options including single homes, duplexes, apartments and rooms for rent. Students wishing to live off-campus need to research availability on their own and should arrive well before the start of term to do so.

Homestay

There are a wide variety of homestay options available, and our partners do their best to match students and hosts according to their interests and preferences. Homestay hosts include single people, young couples with children and pets, and older couples. All homestay accommodations have been inspected, and all adults in the home have completed a required criminal reference check.

university-of-winchester.about:
The University of Winchester is a renowned educational institution with a 185-year history of academic excellence. It is ranked among the Top 15 for graduates in employment and/or further study (in England, Graduate Outcomes Survey 2025, HESA). The campus offers a dynamic academic environment, providing a diverse range of postgraduate and undergraduate courses. Focused on providing excellence in teaching, class sizes are small, with the aim of giving students an outstanding student experience.

Located in the historic city of Winchester, this beautiful self-contained campus boasts a welcoming, community feel, offering first-class, sustainable facilities for learning, teaching and student life. Its convenient location is within easy walking distance of Winchester city centre.

With its medieval architecture and charming streets, this quintessential English city has a rich heritage with lots to offer. Winchester offers students a safe and secure environment, ranked Top 5 safest university cities in England and Wales, Complete University Guide, 2023.

Winchester provides good transport links throughout the United Kingdom, allowing students to enjoy the convenience of direct lines to London in under one hour. The city centre is an easy walk from the University of Winchester campus, and students can explore the Great Hall with King Arthur’s Round Table, the Winchester Cathedral and other nearby attractions.

Why University of Winchester (UoW)

  • Location: Situated in Hampshire, South East England, the vibrant city of Winchester offers a lively contemporary culture, including a thriving arts scene, independent shops, cafes, and restaurants. This welcoming city provides a unique and enriching student experience.
  • Student Support: Winchester Students’ Union is designed to support and represent students every step of the way. It is a democratically elected organisation, run by students for students. The Union plays a crucial role in university life, campaigning on important issues and helping to champion students' rights, as well as providing social and recreational spaces and events to enhance student experience. The Students’ Union Advice Centre is independent from the University and is able to provide free, impartial advice on a range of issues that may be impacting the university experience.
  • Employability: The University works with a range of local, national and international organisations who are keen to access student talent and employ graduates. Ranked top 15 for graduates in employment and/or further study in England, the University of Winchester holds regular careers events and panels where students can build industry networks and gain a better understanding of where their degrees could take them.
  • Sport: Whether a student is trying something new or continuing a life-long passion, Winchester Students’ Union offers more than 30 sports clubs from badminton to basketball, climbing to cricket and tennis to trampolining. Elite athletes can develop and compete in their sport while studying for their degree on the Elite Sport Programme. Students will be provided with expert coaching, sport science support and academic support within an elite sport environment.

university-of-the-west-of-england-bristo.about:
The University of the West of England (UWE) Bristol’s International College offers pathway courses in partnership with UWE Bristol, and is integrated into the University campus. The College is fully equipped to help students prepare for their university degree. With dedicated and experienced staff and outstanding facilities, students will be supported at every step as they start their path to university. Students at UWE Bristol’s International College can choose from a number of courses, with progression to undergraduate or postgraduate degrees.

A pathway course at UWE Bristol's International College (UWEBIC) will provide students with the skills they need to study a degree course at UWE Bristol. As well as English language study, students will learn academic and subject-based skills to help them prepare for university. The College has three pathway options available to students: Foundation Year, International Year One, and Pre-Masters. If students successfully complete their pathway course at the required level, they are guaranteed entry to their chosen undergraduate or postgraduate degrees at UWE Bristol.

Why University of the West of England (UWE) Bristol International College

  • Location: Bristol is a beautiful city with a lively harbourside area, where students will find lots of cafés and restaurants overlooking the water. Students will find lots of street art here, as well as plenty of museums, art galleries, shops and parks.
  • Fantastic Facilities: The College is equipped with everything students need for their studies, and from the first day students will have access to UWE Bristol's advanced facilities like a production studio, and the UK's largest robotics lab, as well as the amenities of the Students' Union.
  • Comprehensive Support: The College's friendly staff will be ready to help students with any problems they may have, whether it's studying for exams or coping with homesickness. They'll also organize fun events for international students, so they can see more of the city and make friends.
